title.zh: 卷69 列傳第34 王劭 袁充
title.en: Volume 69 Biographies 34: Wang Shao, Yuan Chong
title.raw: 卷69 列傳第34 王劭 袁充 Volume 69 Biographies 34: Wang Shao, Yuan Chong

sentences.zh: 王劭王劭字君懋，太原晉陽人也。

translations.literal: Wang Shao—Wang Shao's style name was Junmao—and he was a man of Jinyang in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shao, whose style name was Junmao, came from Jinyang in Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 父松年，齊通直散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: His father Songnian was a Tongzhi attendant cavalier attendant-in-ordinary of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Songnian had served the Northern Qi as a Tongzhi Attendant Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 劭少沈默，好讀書。

translations.literal: Shao in youth was silent and reserved, and loved reading books.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Shao was quiet and reserved and devoted himself to reading.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，齊尚書僕射魏收辟參開府軍事，累遷太子舍人，待詔文林館。

translations.literal: At weak-crown age, Qi Minister of the Works Wei Shou recruited him as staff for the opening of the government, and he was repeatedly promoted to Crown Prince Attendant, awaiting orders at the Wulin Hall.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he was recruited by the Northern Qi Minister of the Works Wei Shou as staff on the opening of the government, rose through several posts to Crown Prince Attendant, and served as a writer awaiting orders at the Wulin Hall.

sentences.zh: 時祖孝徵、魏收、陽休之等嘗論古事，有所遺忘，討閱不能得，因呼劭問之。

translations.literal: At that time Zu Xiaozheng, Wei Shou, Yang Xiuzhi, and others would discuss ancient matters; when something was forgotten and search and review could not recover it, they would call Shao and ask him.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Xiaozheng, Wei Shou, Yang Xiuzhi, and others often discussed antiquity; when some point slipped their memory and searching the texts failed to recover it, they would summon Shao and put the question to him.

sentences.zh: 劭具論所出，取書驗之，一無舛誤。

translations.literal: Shao fully set forth where each item came from; they took books to verify, and there was not a single error.
translations.idiomatic: Shao would cite each passage in full; when they checked against the books, not a single citation proved wrong.

sentences.zh: 自是大為時人所許，稱其博物。

translations.literal: From this he was greatly approved by men of the time, who called him broadly learned.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter contemporaries held him in high regard and praised his encyclopedic learning.

sentences.zh: 後遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to Central Secretariat Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted to Attendant of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 齊滅，入周，不得調。

translations.literal: When Qi perished he entered Zhou but could not obtain an appointment.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of Qi he entered Zhou service but received no posting.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，授著作佐郎。

translations.literal: When Gaozu received the abdication, he was appointed Assistant Gentleman of the Writings.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu took the throne, Shao was appointed Assistant Gentleman of the Writings.

sentences.zh: 以母憂去職，在家著齊書。

translations.literal: On account of mourning for his mother he left office and at home composed the History of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to observe mourning for his mother and at home wrote a history of Qi.

sentences.zh: 時制禁私撰史，為內史侍郎李元操所奏。

translations.literal: At the time regulations forbade private composition of histories, and he was impeached by Internal History Vice Minister Li Yuancao.
translations.idiomatic: Private historical writing was then forbidden by statute, and Internal History Vice Minister Li Yuancao reported him.

sentences.zh: 上怒，遣使收其書，覽而悅之。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and sent an envoy to seize his book; he perused it and was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry and sent men to confiscate the manuscript, but on reading it he was delighted.

sentences.zh: 於是起為員外散騎侍郎，修起居注。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was raised to Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and compiled the Imperial Diary.
translations.idiomatic: He was then recalled as Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and put in charge of the imperial diary.

sentences.zh: 劭以古有鑽燧改火之義，近代廢絕，於是上表請變火，曰：「臣謹案周官，四時變火，以救時疾。

translations.literal: Shao, because antiquity had the meaning of drilling fire and changing fire, while in recent times it had been abandoned, thereupon submitted a memorial requesting change of fire, saying: 'Your servant respectfully examines the Offices of Zhou: in the four seasons fire is changed to relieve seasonal illness.'
translations.idiomatic: Shao noted that antiquity prescribed drilling new fire and changing the hearth fire each season, a practice long since abandoned in recent times, and submitted a memorial asking that the rite be restored: 'Your servant finds in the Offices of Zhou that fire was changed in each of the four seasons to ward off seasonal illness.'

sentences.zh: 明火不數變，時疾必興。

translations.literal: If the bright fire is not changed repeatedly, seasonal illness is sure to arise.
translations.idiomatic: When the hearth fire is not renewed in season, epidemic illness is sure to follow.

sentences.zh: 聖人作法，豈徒然也！

translations.literal: When the sages established the law, was it in vain!
translations.idiomatic: The sages did not establish such rites for nothing!

sentences.zh: 在晉時，有以洛陽火渡江者，代代事之，相續不滅，火色變青。

translations.literal: In Jin times there was one who carried Luoyang fire across the river; generation after generation they served it, continuing unextinguished, and the fire's color turned blue.
translations.idiomatic: In Jin times someone carried the fire of Luoyang across the Yangzi; for generations the household tended it without interruption until the flame turned blue.

sentences.zh: 昔師曠食飯，云是勞薪所爨。

translations.literal: Formerly when Shi Kuang ate his meal, he said it had been cooked with toiling firewood.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago, when the musician Shi Kuang tasted his rice, he declared it had been cooked with overworked firewood.

sentences.zh: 晉平公使視之，果然車輞。

translations.literal: Duke Ping of Jin sent someone to look, and indeed it was a carriage rim.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Ping of Jin sent men to investigate and found it was indeed a carriage wheel rim.

sentences.zh: 今溫酒及炙肉，用石炭、柴火、竹火、草火、麻荄火，氣味各不同。

translations.literal: Now in warming wine and broiling meat, if one uses coal, firewood fire, bamboo fire, grass fire, and hemp-stalk fire, the odors each differ.
translations.idiomatic: Today, when wine is warmed or meat broiled over coal, wood, bamboo, grass, or hemp-stalk fires, each fuel imparts a distinct flavor.

sentences.zh: 以此推之，新火舊火，理應有異。

translations.literal: By this to infer it, new fire and old fire, in principle ought to differ.
translations.idiomatic: From this one may infer that new fire and old fire ought by nature to differ.

sentences.zh: 伏願遠遵先聖，於五時取五木以變火，用功甚少，救益方大。

translations.literal: Your servant humbly wishes to follow far the former sages, and in the five seasons take the five woods to change fire—the effort would be very small, the benefit of relief very great.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant humbly asks that the court follow the ancient sages and, in each of the five seasons, kindle fire from the prescribed five woods—the labor would be slight, the benefit to public health immense.

sentences.zh: 縱使百姓習久，未能頓同，尚食內厨及東宮諸主食厨，不可不依古法。

translations.literal: Even if the common people, long accustomed, could not at once be uniform, the Imperial Provisioner's inner kitchens and the Eastern Palace's various chief kitchens must not fail to follow the ancient law.
translations.idiomatic: Even if the people, long habituated to the old ways, could not change all at once, the imperial kitchens and every chief kitchen of the Eastern Palace should still observe the ancient rule.

sentences.zh: 」上從之。

translations.literal: ' The emperor followed it.
translations.idiomatic: ' The emperor approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 劭又言上有龍顏戴干之表，指示羣臣。

translations.literal: Shao also said that above there was the dragon countenance and the 'bearing shield on the back' physiognomy, and pointed it out to the assembled ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Shao also declared that the emperor bore the dragon countenance and the physiognomic mark of 'bearing the shield on the back,' and pointed these out to the assembled ministers.

sentences.zh: 上大悅，賜物數百段。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and bestowed several hundred lengths of goods.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and rewarded him with several hundred bolts of silk and other goods.

sentences.zh: 拜著作郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed Gentleman of the Writings.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Gentleman of the Writings.

sentences.zh: 劭上表言符命曰：

translations.literal: Shao submitted a memorial speaking of portents and mandate, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Shao submitted a memorial on portents and the Mandate of Heaven, which read:

sentences.zh: :昔周保定二年，歲在壬午，五月五日，青州黃河變清，十里鏡澈，齊氏以為己瑞，改元曰河清。

translations.literal: Formerly in the second year of Baoding of Zhou, the year standing in renwu, on the fifth day of the fifth month, the Yellow River in Qing Province turned clear for ten li like a mirror, and the Qi house took it as their own auspice and changed the era name to Heqing.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Northern Zhou's Baoding reign, a renwu year, on the fifth day of the fifth month the Yellow River in Qing Province ran clear for ten li like polished bronze; the Qi court took this as its own omen and changed the era name to Heqing ('River Clear').

sentences.zh: 是月，至尊以大興公始作隋州刺史，歷年二十，隋果大興。

translations.literal: That month the Supreme One, as Duke of Daxing, first became governor of Sui Province; after twenty years Sui indeed rose greatly.
translations.idiomatic: That same month His Majesty, then Duke of Daxing, first took office as governor of Sui Province; twenty years later the house of Sui rose to greatness as the omen foretold.

sentences.zh: 臣謹案易坤靈圖曰：「聖人受命，瑞先見於河。

translations.literal: Your servant respectfully examines the Changes' Kun Spirit Chart, which says: 'When the sage receives the mandate, the auspice first appears in the river.'
translations.idiomatic: Your servant finds in the Kun Spirit Chart of the Changes: 'When the sage receives the Mandate, the omen appears first in the river.'

sentences.zh: 河者最濁，未能清也。

translations.literal: The river is the most turbid and cannot become clear.
translations.idiomatic: The river is the murkiest of waters and cannot of itself become clear.

sentences.zh: 」竊以靈貺休祥，理無虛發，河清啟聖，實屬大隋。

translations.literal: ' Your servant ventures that numinous gifts and felicitous omens, in principle, are not sent forth in vain; the river's clearing heralded the sage, and in truth it belongs to Great Sui.
translations.idiomatic: ' Such numinous blessings do not appear without cause; the clearing of the river heralded a sage, and that sage was in truth the house of Sui.

sentences.zh: 午為鶉火，以明火德，仲夏火王，亦明火德。

translations.literal: Wu is the Quail Fire asterism, thereby manifesting the Fire Virtue; midsummer is when Fire is king, also manifesting the Fire Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The day wu belongs to the Quail Fire asterism and thus manifests the Fire Virtue; midsummer is the season when Fire reigns, again manifesting the Fire Virtue.

sentences.zh: 月五日五，合天數地數，既得受命之辰，允當先見之兆。

translations.literal: The month's five and day's five combine Heaven's number and Earth's number; having already obtained the time of receiving the mandate, it is fitting that the prior-seen omen should appear.
translations.idiomatic: The fifth month on the fifth day unites Heaven's number and Earth's number; having already fixed the moment of receiving the Mandate, it was only fitting that the omen should appear beforehand.

sentences.zh: :開皇初，邵州人楊令悊近河，得青石圖一，紫石圖一，皆隱起成文，有至尊名，下云：「八方天心。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang, Yang Lingti of Shao Prefecture, near the river, obtained one green stone chart and one purple stone chart, both with raised writing, bearing the Supreme One's name, below saying: 'Eight directions, Heaven's heart.'
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaihuang reign, Yang Lingti of Shao Prefecture found by the river a green stone chart and a purple stone chart, each bearing raised inscriptions including the Supreme One's name and the words 'Eight directions, Heaven's heart.'

sentences.zh: 」永州又得石圖，剖為兩段，有楊樹之形，黃根紫葉。

translations.literal: ' Yong Prefecture again obtained a stone chart split into two sections, with the form of a poplar tree, yellow roots and purple leaves.
translations.idiomatic: ' Yong Prefecture also produced a stone chart split in two, shaped like a poplar with yellow roots and purple leaves.

sentences.zh: 汝水得神龜，腹下有文曰：「天卜楊興。

translations.literal: The Ru River obtained a divine turtle; beneath its belly was writing saying: 'Heaven divines: Yang shall rise.'
translations.idiomatic: At the Ru River a divine turtle appeared with characters on its belly reading 'Heaven divines: the house of Yang shall rise.'

sentences.zh: 」安邑掘地，得古鐵版，文曰：「皇始天年，賚楊鐵券，王興。

translations.literal: ' At Anyi they dug the earth and obtained an ancient iron plate; the writing said: 'Imperial beginning, Heaven's year—bestow on Yang an iron tally: the king shall rise.'
translations.idiomatic: ' At Anyi diggers unearthed an ancient iron plate inscribed 'Imperial beginning, Heaven's year—grant Yang the iron tally: the king shall rise.'

sentences.zh: 」同州得石龜，文曰：「天子延千年，大吉。

translations.literal: ' Tong Prefecture obtained a stone turtle; the writing said: 'The Son of Heaven extends a thousand years—great auspice.'
translations.idiomatic: ' Tong Prefecture yielded a stone turtle inscribed 'The Son of Heaven shall endure a thousand years—great good fortune.'

sentences.zh: 」臣以前之三石，不異龍圖。

translations.literal: ' Your servant considers the former three stones no different from the dragon chart.
translations.idiomatic: ' Your servant holds that these three stone omens are no different from the dragon chart of old.

sentences.zh: 何以用石？

translations.literal: Why use stone?
translations.idiomatic: Why were stone omens chosen?

sentences.zh: 石鐵久固，義與上名符合。

translations.literal: Stone and iron endure long and firm; the meaning matches the Supreme One's name.
translations.idiomatic: Stone and iron are enduring and firm, matching the meaning of the Supreme One's name.

sentences.zh: 龜腹七字，何以著龜？

translations.literal: Seven characters on the turtle's belly—why inscribe them on a turtle?
translations.idiomatic: Why were the seven characters inscribed on a turtle's belly?

sentences.zh: 龜亦久固，兼是神靈之物。

translations.literal: The turtle also endures long and firm, and moreover is a numinous thing.
translations.idiomatic: The turtle too is long-lived and firm, and besides is a numinous creature.

sentences.zh: 孔子歎河不出圖，洛不出書，今於大隋聖世，圖書屢出。

translations.literal: Confucius sighed that the river did not yield a chart and the Luo did not yield a book; now in the holy age of Great Sui, charts and books repeatedly appear.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius lamented that the river yielded no chart and the Luo no book; yet in the sacred age of Great Sui such charts and books appear again and again.

sentences.zh: :建德六年，亳州大周村有龍鬬，白者勝，黑者死。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Jiande, at Dazhou Village in Bozhou there was a dragon fight; the white one prevailed, the black one died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Jiande, at Dazhou Village in Bozhou two dragons fought; the white dragon won and the black dragon died.

sentences.zh: 大象元年夏，熒陽汴水北有龍鬬，初見白氣屬天，自東方歷陽武而來。

translations.literal: In summer of the first year of Daxiang, north of the Bian River at Yingyang there was a dragon fight; at first white vapor reached the sky, coming from the east through Yangwu.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the first year of Daxiang, north of the Bian River at Yingyang, dragons fought again; at first white vapor rose to the sky, advancing from the east through Yangwu.

sentences.zh: 及至，白龍也，長十許丈。

translations.literal: When it arrived, it was a white dragon, more than ten zhang long.
translations.idiomatic: When it drew near, it proved to be a white dragon some ten zhang in length.

sentences.zh: 有黑龍乘雲而至，兩相薄，乍合乍離，自午至申，白龍升天，黑龍墜地。

translations.literal: A black dragon came riding clouds; the two pressed on each other, now joining now parting; from the wu hour to the shen hour the white dragon ascended to heaven and the black dragon fell to earth.
translations.idiomatic: A black dragon came on clouds to meet it; the two closed and broke apart from noon until mid-afternoon, when the white dragon rose into heaven and the black dragon fell to earth.

sentences.zh: 謹案：龍，君象也。

translations.literal: Respectfully examined: the dragon is the image of the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant notes: the dragon is the image of the ruler.

sentences.zh: 前鬬於亳州周村者，蓋象至尊以龍鬬之歲為亳州總管，遂代周有天下。

translations.literal: The earlier fight at Zhou Village in Bozhou likely images that the Supreme One, in the year of the dragon fight, was Bozhou governor-general and thereafter replaced Zhou and possessed the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The earlier fight at Zhou Village in Bozhou surely foreshadowed that His Majesty, in the very year of the dragon fight, was governor-general of Bozhou and would thereafter supplant Zhou and win the realm.

sentences.zh: 後鬬於熒陽者，「熒」字三火，明火德之盛也。

translations.literal: The later fight at Yingyang: the character 'ying' has three fires, clearly manifesting the abundance of the Fire Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The later fight at Yingyang: the character ying contains three 'fire' elements, plainly manifesting the fullness of the Fire Virtue.

sentences.zh: 白龍從東方來，歷陽武者，蓋象至尊將登帝位，從東第入自崇陽門也。

translations.literal: The white dragon coming from the east, passing Yangwu, likely images that the Supreme One, about to ascend the imperial throne, would enter from the eastern residence through the Chongyang Gate.
translations.idiomatic: The white dragon coming from the east through Yangwu surely images His Majesty's ascent to the throne, entering from the eastern residence through the Chongyang Gate.

sentences.zh: 西北升天者，當乾位天門。

translations.literal: Ascending to heaven in the northwest corresponds to the Qian position, Heaven's Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Its ascent to the northwest corresponds to the Qian trigram—the Gate of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 坤靈圖曰：「聖人殺龍。

translations.literal: The Kun Spirit Chart says: 'The sage slays the dragon.'
translations.idiomatic: The Kun Spirit Chart says: 'The sage slays the dragon.'

sentences.zh: 」龍不可得而殺，皆盛氣也。

translations.literal: ' Dragons cannot be obtained and slain—they are all flourishing qi.
translations.idiomatic: ' Dragons cannot truly be killed; both are manifestations of flourishing cosmic force.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「泰姓商名宮，黃色，長八尺，六十世，河龍以正月辰見，白龍與五黑龍鬬，白龍陵，故泰人有命。

translations.literal: It also says: 'Tai: surname Shang, name Gong, yellow color, eight chi tall, sixty generations; the river dragon appears in the first month at chen; the white dragon fights five black dragons; the white dragon prevails—therefore the Tai people have the mandate.'
translations.idiomatic: It also says: 'Tai: surname Shang, personal name Gong, yellow in color, eight chi in stature, sixty generations; the river dragon appears in the first month at the chen hour; the white dragon battles five black dragons and prevails—thus the Tai people receive the Mandate.'

sentences.zh: 」謹案：此言皆為大隋而發也。

translations.literal: ' Your servant respectfully examines: these words were all issued for Great Sui.
translations.idiomatic: ' Your servant finds that every phrase was uttered for the house of Sui.

sentences.zh: 聖人殺龍者，前後龍死是也。

translations.literal: 'The sage slaying the dragon' means the dragons dying before and after.
translations.idiomatic: 'The sage slays the dragon' refers to the deaths of the dragons in both encounters.

sentences.zh: 姓商者，皇家於五姓為商也。

translations.literal: 'Surname Shang' means the imperial house among the five surnames is Shang.
translations.idiomatic: 'Surname Shang' means that among the five tones the imperial clan corresponds to Shang.

sentences.zh: 名宮者，武元皇帝諱於五聲為宮。

translations.literal: 'Name Gong' means Emperor Wuyuan's taboo name among the five sounds is gong.
translations.idiomatic: 'Name Gong' means that Emperor Wuyuan's taboo name falls under the gong pitch of the five tones.

sentences.zh: 黃色者，隋色尚黃。

translations.literal: 'Yellow color' means Sui esteems yellow.
translations.idiomatic: 'Yellow' means that Sui honors the yellow color.

sentences.zh: 長八尺者，武元皇帝身長八尺。

translations.literal: 'Eight chi tall' means Emperor Wuyuan's body was eight chi.
translations.idiomatic: 'Eight chi in stature' refers to Emperor Wuyuan, who stood eight chi tall.

sentences.zh: 河龍以正月辰見者，泰正月卦，龍見之所，於京師為辰地。

translations.literal: 'The river dragon appearing in the first month at chen'—Tai is the first-month hexagram; where the dragon appears, in the capital it is the chen position.
translations.idiomatic: 'The river dragon appears in the first month at chen'—Tai is the hexagram of the first month, and the place of the dragon's appearance in the capital corresponds to the chen direction.

sentences.zh: 白龍與黑龍鬬者，亳州熒陽龍鬬是也。

translations.literal: 'The white dragon fighting the black dragon' is the dragon fights at Bozhou and Yingyang.
translations.idiomatic: 'The white dragon battles the black dragon' refers to the fights at Bozhou and Yingyang.

sentences.zh: 勝龍所以白者，楊姓納音為商，至尊又辛酉歲生，位皆在西方，西方色白也。

translations.literal: Why the victorious dragon was white: the Yang surname's received tone is shang; the Supreme One was also born in a xinyou year; both positions are in the west, and the west's color is white.
translations.idiomatic: The victorious dragon was white because the Yang clan's received tone is shang, His Majesty was born in a xinyou year, and both stand in the west, whose color is white.

sentences.zh: 死龍所以黑者，周色黑。

translations.literal: Why the dead dragon was black: Zhou's color was black.
translations.idiomatic: The defeated dragon was black because Zhou honored black.

sentences.zh: 所以稱五者，周閔、明、武、宣、靖凡五帝。

translations.literal: Why it says five: the Zhou emperors Min, Ming, Wu, Xuan, and Jing—five emperors in all.
translations.idiomatic: The 'five' refers to the five Zhou emperors Min, Ming, Wu, Xuan, and Jing.

sentences.zh: 趙、陳、代、越、滕五王，一時伏法，亦當五數。

translations.literal: The five princes of Zhao, Chen, Dai, Yue, and Teng were executed at one time—also matching the number five.
translations.idiomatic: The five princes of Zhao, Chen, Dai, Yue, and Teng were executed together—again matching the number five.

sentences.zh: 白龍陵者，陵猶勝也。

translations.literal: 'The white dragon prevails (ling)'—ling is like sheng, 'to overcome.'
translations.idiomatic: 'The white dragon ling'—ling means to overcome.

sentences.zh: 鄭玄說：「陵當為除。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan explained: 'Ling should be read as chu.'
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan explained that ling should be read as chu ('to remove').

sentences.zh: 」凡鬬能去敵曰除。

translations.literal: ' In any fight, being able to remove the enemy is called chu.
translations.idiomatic: ' In combat, to drive off the foe is called chu.

sentences.zh: 臣以泰人有命者，泰之為言通也，大也，明其人道通德大，有天命也。

translations.literal: Your servant considers 'the Tai people have the mandate': tai as a word means penetrating and great, showing that their human way penetrates and virtue is great—they have Heaven's mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant holds that 'the Tai people have the mandate' means that tai signifies penetration and greatness—His Majesty's human way is penetrating and his virtue vast, and Heaven's mandate is his.

sentences.zh: 乾鑿度曰：「泰表戴干。

translations.literal: The Qian Aperture Measure says: 'The Tai people's mark bears the shield on the back.'
translations.idiomatic: The Qian Aperture Measure says: 'The mark of the Tai people bears the shield on the back.'

sentences.zh: 」鄭玄注云：「表者，人形體之彰識也。

translations.literal: ' Zheng Xuan annotated: 'Biao is the manifest sign on the human form.'
translations.idiomatic: ' Zheng Xuan glossed it: 'Biao is the visible mark on the human body.'

sentences.zh: 干，盾也。

translations.literal: Gan is a shield.
translations.idiomatic: Gan means shield.

sentences.zh: 泰人之表戴干。

translations.literal: The Tai people's mark bears the shield.
translations.idiomatic: The mark of the Tai people bears the shield on the back.

sentences.zh: 」臣伏見至尊有戴干之表，益知泰人之表不爽毫釐。

translations.literal: ' Your servant humbly sees that the Supreme One has the mark of bearing the shield on the back, and all the more knows that the Tai people's mark does not miss by a hair's breadth.
translations.idiomatic: ' Your servant has seen that His Majesty bears this mark, and knows thereby that the prophecy of the Tai people's mark is exact to the finest detail.

sentences.zh: 坤靈圖所云，字字皆驗。

translations.literal: What the Kun Spirit Chart states—every word is verified.
translations.idiomatic: Every word of the Kun Spirit Chart has been fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 緯書又稱「漢四百年」，終如其言，則知六十世亦必然矣。

translations.literal: The weft books also say 'Han four hundred years,' and in the end it was as they said; thus one knows that sixty generations is also inevitable.
translations.idiomatic: The apocryphal texts also foretold 'four hundred years for Han,' and that came to pass; thus sixty generations for Sui is likewise assured.

sentences.zh: 昔宗周卜世三十，今則倍之。

translations.literal: Formerly the Zhou of the clan divined thirty generations; now it is doubled.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou of old divined thirty generations for their house; Sui's span will be twice that.

sentences.zh: :稽覽圖云：「太平時，陰陽和合，風雨咸同，海內不偏，地有阻險，故風有遲疾。

translations.literal: The Examination Chart says: 'In the age of Great Peace, yin and yang harmonize, wind and rain are alike everywhere, within the seas there is no partiality; because the land has barriers and defiles, therefore winds have slow and fast.'
translations.idiomatic: The Examination Chart says: 'In the age of Great Peace yin and yang are in harmony, wind and rain fall alike throughout the realm, and no region is favored over another; yet where terrain is rugged, winds naturally vary in speed.'

sentences.zh: 雖太平之政，猶有不能均同，唯平均乃不鳴條，故欲風於亳。

translations.literal: Even under the government of Great Peace there are still places that cannot be made uniform; only when averaged is there no rustling of branches—therefore it desires wind at Bo.
translations.idiomatic: Even under perfect government some places cannot be made uniform; only when all is balanced do the branches cease to rustle—hence the prophecy desires wind at Bo.

sentences.zh: 亳者，陳留也。

translations.literal: Bo is Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: Bo is Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 」謹案：此言蓋明至尊者為陳留公世子，亳州總管，遂受天命，海內均同，不偏不黨，以成太平之風化也。

translations.literal: ' Your servant respectfully examines: these words likely show that the Supreme One, as heir of the Duke of Chenliu and Bozhou governor-general, then received Heaven's mandate—the realm uniform and alike, without partiality or faction, thereby accomplishing the transforming influence of Great Peace.
translations.idiomatic: ' Your servant finds that this passage shows His Majesty, as heir of the Duke of Chenliu and as governor-general of Bozhou, received Heaven's mandate and brought the realm into even harmony without partiality, fulfilling the prophecy of Great Peace.

sentences.zh: 在大統十六年，武元皇帝改封陳留公。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Datong, Emperor Wuyuan was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year of Datong, Emperor Wuyuan was enfeoffed as Duke of Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 是時齊國有祕記云：「天王陳留入并州。

translations.literal: At that time the Qi state had a secret record saying: 'The Heavenly King of Chenliu enters Bing Province.'
translations.idiomatic: At that time a secret prophecy in Qi read: 'The Heavenly King of Chenliu will enter Bing Province.'

sentences.zh: 」齊王高洋為是誅陳留王彭樂。

translations.literal: ' For this Qi King Gao Yang executed the Prince of Chenliu, Peng Le.
translations.idiomatic: ' For this reason Qi King Gao Yang executed Peng Le, Prince of Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 其後武元皇帝果將兵入并州。

translations.literal: Afterward Emperor Wuyuan indeed led troops into Bing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Later Emperor Wuyuan did indeed lead an army into Bing Province.

sentences.zh: 周武帝時，望氣者云亳州有天子氣，於是殺亳州刺史紇豆陵恭，至尊代為之。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Wu of Zhou, those who read vapors said Bozhou had the qi of a Son of Heaven; thereupon they killed Bozhou Inspector Hedouling Gong, and the Supreme One replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wu of Zhou, geomancers reported the qi of an emperor at Bozhou; the Zhou court then executed Bozhou Inspector Hedouling Gong, and His Majesty was appointed in his place.

sentences.zh: 又陳留老子祠有枯柏，世傳云老子將度世，云待枯柏生東南枝廻指，當有聖人出，吾道復行。

translations.literal: Also at the Laozi shrine in Chenliu there was a withered cypress; the world transmitted that when Laozi was about to transcend the world he said: wait until the withered cypress puts forth a southeast branch turning back—then a sage will appear and our Way will flourish again.
translations.idiomatic: At the Laozi shrine in Chenliu stood a withered cypress; tradition held that when Laozi was about to leave the world he said that when the tree put forth a southeast branch turning back, a sage would appear and the Way would flourish again.

sentences.zh: 至齊，枯柏從下生枝，東南上指。

translations.literal: By the time of Qi, the withered cypress sprouted branches from below, pointing up to the southeast.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Qi dynasty the withered cypress sprouted new branches from its base, turning toward the southeast.

sentences.zh: 夜有三童子相與歌曰：「老子廟前古枯樹，東南狀如傘，聖主從此去。

translations.literal: At night three boys sang together: 'Before Laozi's temple, the ancient withered tree—southeast shaped like an umbrella; the sage lord departs from here.'
translations.idiomatic: One night three boys were heard singing: 'Before Laozi's temple stands an ancient withered tree, its southeast branches like an umbrella—the sage lord will go forth from here.'

sentences.zh: 」及至尊牧亳州，親至祠樹之下。

translations.literal: ' When the Supreme One governed Bozhou, he personally came beneath the shrine tree.
translations.idiomatic: ' When His Majesty governed Bozhou he came in person to the tree at the shrine.

sentences.zh: 自是柏枝廻抱，其枯枝，漸指西北，道教果行。

translations.literal: From this the cypress branches turned back and embraced; its withered branches gradually pointed northwest, and the Way of the Dao indeed flourished.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the branches curled back upon themselves and the withered limbs slowly turned toward the northwest, and the Daoist teaching did indeed flourish.

sentences.zh: 校考眾事，太平主出於亳州陳留之地，皆如所言。

translations.literal: Comparing and examining the many matters, the lord of Great Peace arising from the land of Bozhou and Chenliu—all was as spoken.
translations.idiomatic: When one compares these events, the lord of Great Peace arising from Bozhou and Chenliu fulfilled every word of the prophecy.

sentences.zh: :稽覽圖又云：「治道得，則陰物變為陽物。

translations.literal: The Examination Chart again says: 'When the way of governance is attained, yin things change into yang things.'
translations.idiomatic: The Examination Chart also says: 'When governance is perfected, yin substances transform into yang substances.'

sentences.zh: 」鄭玄注云：「葱變為韭亦是。

translations.literal: ' Zheng Xuan annotated: 'Scallions changing into leeks is also such a case.'
translations.idiomatic: ' Zheng Xuan glossed this: 'Scallions turning into leeks is an example.'

sentences.zh: 」謹案：自六年以來，遠近山石，多變為玉。

translations.literal: Your servant respectfully examines: since the sixth year, stones near and far have largely turned into jade.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant notes that since the sixth year, jade has appeared in stones throughout the realm, near and far.

sentences.zh: 石為陰，玉為陽。

translations.literal: Stone is yin; jade is yang.
translations.idiomatic: Stone belongs to yin; jade belongs to yang.

sentences.zh: 又左衞園中葱皆變為韭。

translations.literal: Also in the Left Guard garden all scallions turned into leeks.
translations.idiomatic: In the Left Guard's garden, moreover, every scallion had changed into chives.

sentences.zh: 上覽之大悅，賜物五百段。

translations.literal: The emperor, on reading this, was greatly pleased and bestowed five hundred lengths of goods.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor read the report he was delighted and rewarded him with five hundred bolts of goods.

sentences.zh: 未幾，劭復上書曰：

translations.literal: Before long Shao again submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Not long afterward Shao submitted another memorial:

sentences.zh: :易乾鑿度曰：「隨上六，拘係之，乃從維之，王用享于西山。

translations.literal: The Qian Aperture Measure of the Changes says: 'At the top line of Sui: restrain and bind it, then follow and uphold it—the king makes offering at Mount Xi.'
translations.idiomatic: The Qian Aperture Measure reads: 'On the top line of Sui: restrain and bind it, then follow and sustain it—the king performs sacrifice at Mount Xi.'

sentences.zh: 隨者二月卦，陽德施行，藩決難解，萬物隨陽而出。

translations.literal: Sui is the second-month hexagram; yang virtue is put into practice; barriers are opened and difficulties dissolved; all things follow the yang and emerge.
translations.idiomatic: Sui is the hexagram of the second month, when yang virtue goes forth; frontier barriers fall open, hardships dissolve, and the myriad things rise with the yang.

sentences.zh: 故上六欲九五拘係之，維持之，明被陽化而陰隨從之也。

translations.literal: Thus the top line wishes the fifth line to restrain and bind it and uphold it—showing that, having been transformed by yang, yin follows in submission.
translations.idiomatic: The top line therefore seeks the fifth line to restrain, bind, and uphold it—meaning that yin, once transformed by yang, follows in obedience.

sentences.zh: 」易稽覽圖：「坤六月，有子女，任政，一年，傳為復。

translations.literal: The Examination Chart of the Changes: 'In Kun, the sixth month, there are children who hold governance; after one year, it passes to Fu.'
translations.idiomatic: The Examination Chart states: 'Under Kun in the sixth month, a child holds power; after one year, authority passes to Fu.'

sentences.zh: 五月貧之從東北來立，大起土邑，西北地動星墜，陽衞。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Pinzhi comes from the northeast to establish rule; great earthworks for cities are raised; in the northwest the earth quakes and stars fall; Yang guards.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the True Man arrives from the northeast to take the throne; great earthen cities are raised; the northwest quakes and stars fall; Yang stands guard.

sentences.zh: 屯十一月神人從中山出，趙地動。

translations.literal: In Zhun, the eleventh month, a divine man emerges from Zhongshan; the Zhao region quakes.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhun in the eleventh month, a divine man comes forth from Zhongshan, and the land of Zhao trembles.

sentences.zh: 北方三十日，千里馬數至。

translations.literal: In the north, for thirty days, thousand-li horses come repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: For thirty days in the north, horses capable of a thousand li arrive again and again.

sentences.zh: 」謹案：凡此易緯所言，皆是大隋符命。

translations.literal: Your servant respectfully examines: all that these Changes apocrypha say is the mandate-token of Great Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant finds that every passage in these Changes apocrypha prophesies the mandate of Great Sui.

sentences.zh: 隨者二月之卦，明大隋以二月即皇帝位也。

translations.literal: Sui is the second-month hexagram, showing that Great Sui ascended the imperial throne in the second month.
translations.idiomatic: Because Sui is the hexagram of the second month, it shows that Great Sui took the throne in that month.

sentences.zh: 陽德施行者，明楊氏之德教施行於天下也。

translations.literal: Yang virtue is put into practice shows that the Yang clan's virtue and teachings were put into practice throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Yang virtue goes forth reveals that the Yang family's moral teaching spread across the empire.

sentences.zh: 藩決難解者，明當時藩鄣皆是通決，險難皆解散也。

translations.literal: Barriers are opened and difficulties dissolved shows that at that time all frontier defenses were opened through and all dangers dissolved.
translations.idiomatic: Barriers fall open and hardships dissolve means that frontier strongholds were thrown open and every peril was dispelled.

sentences.zh: 萬物隨陽而出者，明天地間萬物盡隨楊氏而出見也。

translations.literal: All things follow the yang and emerge shows that all things in heaven and earth followed the Yang clan to emerge and appear.
translations.idiomatic: The myriad things rise with the yang signifies that everything under heaven came forth in the train of the Yang.

sentences.zh: 上六欲九五拘係之者，五為王，六為宗廟，明宗廟神靈欲令登九五之位，帝王拘民以禮，係民以義也。

translations.literal: The top line wishing the fifth line to restrain and bind it—five is the king, six is the ancestral temple—shows that the spirits of the ancestral temple wished him to ascend the nine-five position; the emperor restrains the people with ritual and binds the people with righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: When the top line seeks the fifth line to restrain and bind it—five being the sovereign, six the ancestral temple—it means the temple spirits wished him to mount the throne; the emperor holds the people with ritual and binds them with righteousness.

sentences.zh: 「拘民以禮」，「係民以義」，此二句亦是乾鑿度之言。

translations.literal: Restrain the people with ritual and bind the people with righteousness—these two phrases are also words from the Qian Aperture Measure.
translations.idiomatic: The lines restrain the people with ritual and bind the people with righteousness likewise come from the Qian Aperture Measure.

sentences.zh: 維持之者，明能以綱維持正天下也。

translations.literal: Uphold it shows that he was able to set the realm right with binding principles.
translations.idiomatic: Sustain it shows that he could govern the realm uprightly through firm moral bonds.

sentences.zh: 被陽化而欲陰隨之者，明陰類被服楊氏之風化，莫不隨從。

translations.literal: Having been transformed by yang and yin following shows that yin categories received the Yang clan's cultural transformation and none failed to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Transformed by yang, yin follows means that all yin things accepted the Yang family's civilizing influence and submitted without exception.

sentences.zh: 陰謂臣下也。

translations.literal: Yin refers to subordinate officials.
translations.idiomatic: By yin is meant the officials below the throne.

sentences.zh: 王用享于西山者，蓋明至尊常以歲二月幸西山仁壽宮也。

translations.literal: The king makes offering at Mount Xi presumably shows that the Supreme One regularly in the second month of the year visited the Renshou Palace at Mount Xi.
translations.idiomatic: The king sacrifices at Mount Xi surely indicates that His Majesty each year in the second month visited the Renshou Palace on Mount Xi.

sentences.zh: 凡四稱隨，三稱陽，欲美隋楊，丁寧之至也。

translations.literal: In all, Sui is mentioned four times and Yang three times—wishing to praise Sui and Yang to the utmost degree of earnest repetition.
translations.idiomatic: Four times the text says Sui and three times Yang—as if repeating the names of Sui and Yang again and again in the most earnest praise.

sentences.zh: 坤六月者，坤位在未，六月建未，言至尊以六月生也。

translations.literal: Kun, the sixth month—Kun's position is at wei; the sixth month is established at wei—meaning the Supreme One was born in the sixth month.
translations.idiomatic: Kun in the sixth month places Kun in the wei position, and the sixth month is keyed to wei—showing that His Majesty was born in the sixth month.

sentences.zh: 有子女任政者，言樂平公主是皇帝子女，而為周后，任理內政也。

translations.literal: There are children who hold governance means that Princess Leping was the emperor's daughter, yet became Empress of Zhou and managed internal affairs.
translations.idiomatic: A child holds power refers to Princess Leping, the emperor's own daughter, who became Empress of Zhou and governed the inner court.

sentences.zh: 一年傳為復者，復是坤之一世卦，陽氣初起，言周宣帝崩後一年，傳位與楊氏也。

translations.literal: After one year, it passes to Fu—Fu is one of Kun's generational hexagrams, when yang qi first rises—meaning one year after Emperor Xuan of Zhou died, the throne passed to the Yang clan.
translations.idiomatic: After one year, authority passes to Fu—Fu being Kun's generational hexagram, when yang first stirs—means that one year after Emperor Xuan of Zhou's death the throne passed to the Yang.

sentences.zh: 五月貧之從東北來立者，「貧之」當為「真人」，字之誤也。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Pinzhi comes from the northeast to establish rule—Pinzhi should be True Man, a textual error in the characters.
translations.idiomatic: In the line In the fifth month, Pinzhi comes from the northeast to take the throne, Pinzhi is a mistaken writing for True Man.

sentences.zh: 言周宣帝以五月崩，真人革命，當在此時。

translations.literal: It means that Emperor Xuan of Zhou died in the fifth month, and the True Man's revolution should have occurred at this time.
translations.idiomatic: The meaning is that when Emperor Xuan of Zhou died in the fifth month, the True Man's revolution ought to have begun then.

sentences.zh: 至尊謙讓而逆天意，故踰年乃立。

translations.literal: The Supreme One was modest and deferential and went against Heaven's intent, and therefore was enthroned only after a year had passed.
translations.idiomatic: His Majesty, out of humility, deferred against Heaven's will and therefore did not ascend the throne until a full year had passed.

sentences.zh: 昔為定州總管，在京師東北，本而言之，故曰真人從東北來立。

translations.literal: He had formerly been regional commander of Dingzhou, northeast of the capital—in origin it was thus said that the True Man came from the northeast to establish rule.
translations.idiomatic: Since he had once served as commander of Dingzhou, northeast of the capital, the text in its original sense says that the True Man came from the northeast to take the throne.

sentences.zh: 大起土邑者，大起即大興，言營大興城邑也。

translations.literal: Great earthworks for cities—Daqi is Daxing, meaning the construction of the city of Daxing.
translations.idiomatic: Great earthworks for cities—Daqi stands for Daxing—refers to the building of the great city of Daxing.

sentences.zh: 西北地動星墜者，蓋天意去周授隋，故變動也。

translations.literal: In the northwest the earth quakes and stars fall—presumably Heaven's intent was to remove Zhou and grant rule to Sui, hence the disturbances.
translations.idiomatic: The northwest quakes and stars fall shows Heaven casting off Zhou and bestowing the mandate upon Sui, hence the upheavals.

sentences.zh: 陽衞者，言楊氏得天衞助。

translations.literal: Yang guards means the Yang clan received the aid of Heaven's guards.
translations.idiomatic: Yang guards means the Yang received the protection of Heaven's celestial guard.

sentences.zh: 屯十一月神人從中山出者，此卦動而大亨作，故至尊以十一月被授亳州總管，將從中山而出也。

translations.literal: In Zhun, the eleventh month, a divine man emerges from Zhongshan—this hexagram stirs and great success is achieved, hence the Supreme One in the eleventh month was appointed regional commander of Bozhou, about to emerge from Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhun in the eleventh month, a divine man comes from Zhongshan—the hexagram moves and great fortune arises—so in the eleventh month His Majesty was made commander of Bozhou and was about to go forth from Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 趙地動者，中山為趙地，以神人將去，故變動也。

translations.literal: The Zhao region quakes—Zhongshan is the Zhao region; because the divine man was about to depart, there was disturbance.
translations.idiomatic: The land of Zhao trembles because Zhongshan lies in Zhao; as the divine man was leaving, the earth shook.

sentences.zh: 北方三十日者，蓋至尊從北方將往亳州之時，停留三十日也。

translations.literal: In the north, for thirty days—presumably when the Supreme One was traveling from the north toward Bozhou, he stayed for thirty days.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty days in the north means that when His Majesty traveled south from the north toward Bozhou, he halted there for thirty days.

sentences.zh: 千里馬者，蓋至尊舊所乘騧騮馬也。

translations.literal: Thousand-li horses—presumably the piebald horse the Supreme One formerly rode.
translations.idiomatic: Horses of a thousand li refers to the piebald stallion His Majesty once rode.

sentences.zh: 屯卦震下坎上，震於馬作足，坎於馬為美脊，是故騧騮馬脊有肉鞍，行則先作弄四足也。

translations.literal: The Zhun hexagram has Zhen below and Kan above; Zhen in horses signifies stamping feet, Kan in horses signifies a fine back—hence the piebald horse's back had a fleshy saddle, and when it walked it first pranced with all four legs.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhun, Zhen lies below and Kan above; Zhen governs a horse's stamping feet, Kan its noble back—hence the piebald's spine bore a fleshy saddle, and when it moved it first danced on all four hooves.

sentences.zh: 數至者，言曆數至也。

translations.literal: Come repeatedly means the calendrical count had arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Arrive again and again means that the destined number of years had come due.

sentences.zh: :河圖帝通紀曰：「形瑞出，變矩衡。

translations.literal: The River Chart's Emperor Communication Record says: 'Auspicious forms appear; the square and balance are transformed.'
translations.idiomatic: The River Chart's Emperor Communication Record declares: 'Portents take shape; the square and the balance are transformed.'

sentences.zh: 赤應隨，協靈皇。

translations.literal: Red responds to Sui; harmony with the Spirit Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Crimson answers Sui; accord with the Spirit Emperor.

sentences.zh: 」河圖皇參持曰：「皇辟出，承元訖。

translations.literal: The River Chart's Imperial Canopy Holder says: 'The great sovereign emerges; he inherits the end of the Primordial Cycle.'
translations.idiomatic: The River Chart's Imperial Canopy Holder reads: 'The great sovereign comes forth; he succeeds when the Primordial Cycle ends.'

sentences.zh: 道無為，治率。

translations.literal: The Way is non-action; governance leads the masses.
translations.idiomatic: The Way is effortless; rule guides all beneath Heaven.

sentences.zh: 被遂矩，戲作術。

translations.literal: Clothed in Sui's square; playfully creating the art.
translations.idiomatic: Invested with Sui's measure; devising the sacred arts in sport.

sentences.zh: 開皇色，握神日。

translations.literal: Kaihuang color; grasping the divine sun.
translations.idiomatic: The hue of Kaihuang; holding fast to the divine sun.

sentences.zh: 投輔提，象不絕。

translations.literal: Entrusting to assistants to lead; the symbols are unbroken.
translations.idiomatic: Power is handed to ministers to bear up; the patterns of rule never cease.

sentences.zh: 立皇後，翼不格。

translations.literal: Establishing the imperial heir; the winged helpers do not reach.
translations.idiomatic: An heir is installed; yet those who should support him fall short.

sentences.zh: 道終始，德優劣。

translations.literal: The Way ends and begins; virtue has superior and inferior.
translations.idiomatic: One Way closes, another opens; virtue knows both decline and renewal.

sentences.zh: 帝任政，河曲出。

translations.literal: The emperor personally governs; the river bend produces a sign.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor himself takes up rule; a chart emerges from the river's bend.

sentences.zh: 協輔嬉，爛可述。

translations.literal: Harmonious assistants rejoice; splendor worth recounting.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers unite in glad service; glory bright enough to be sung.

sentences.zh: 」謹案：凡此河圖所言，亦是大隋符命。

translations.literal: Your servant respectfully examines: all that these River Chart texts say is likewise the mandate-token of Great Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant finds that everything written in these River Charts likewise prophesies the mandate of Great Sui.

sentences.zh: 形瑞出、變矩衡者，矩，法也，衡，北斗星名，所謂璿璣玉衡者也。

translations.literal: Auspicious forms appear and the square and balance are transformed—ju is law; heng is the name of a Big Dipper star, what is called the xuanji jade balance.
translations.idiomatic: Portents take shape and the square and balance change—ju means law, heng is a star of the Northern Dipper, the so-called Xuanji Jade Balance.

sentences.zh: 大隋受命，形兆之瑞始出，天象則為之變動。

translations.literal: When Great Sui received the mandate, auspicious omens first appeared, and the celestial signs changed accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: When Great Sui received Heaven's mandate, earthly omens first appeared and the heavens altered their signs in response.

sentences.zh: 北斗主天之法度，故曰矩衡。

translations.literal: The Big Dipper governs Heaven's standards of measure, hence it is called ju and heng.
translations.idiomatic: Because the Northern Dipper presides over Heaven's standards, the text calls them ju and heng.

sentences.zh: 易緯「伏戲矩衡神」，鄭玄注亦以為法玉衡之神。

translations.literal: The Changes apocrypha phrase Fuxi's square-and-balance god—Zheng Xuan's commentary likewise takes it as the god of law and the jade balance.
translations.idiomatic: In the Changes apocrypha, Fuxi's square-and-balance spirit—Zheng Xuan's commentary likewise interprets it as the spirit of law and the jade balance.

sentences.zh: 與此河圖矩衡義同。

translations.literal: The meaning is the same as ju and heng in this River Chart text.
translations.idiomatic: That meaning matches ju and heng in this River Chart passage.

sentences.zh: 赤應隋者，言赤帝降精，感應而生隋也。

translations.literal: Red responds to Sui means the Red Emperor descended his essence, and through resonance Sui was born.
translations.idiomatic: Crimson answers Sui means the Red Emperor sent down his essence and, through that resonance, Sui arose.

sentences.zh: 故隋以火德為赤帝天子。

translations.literal: Therefore Sui took fire as its virtue and became the Son of Heaven of the Red Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Hence Sui claimed the virtue of fire and became the Son of Heaven of the Red Emperor.

sentences.zh: 協靈皇者，協，合也，言大隋德合上靈天皇大帝也。

translations.literal: Harmony with the Spirit Emperor—xie means accord; it means Great Sui's virtue accorded with the Great Spirit Heavenly Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Accord with the Spirit Emperor—xie means harmony—shows that Great Sui's virtue aligned with the Great Spirit Heavenly Emperor.

sentences.zh: 又年號開皇，與靈寶經之開皇年相合，故曰協靈皇。

translations.literal: Moreover the era name Kaihuang accorded with the Kaihuang year in the Lingbao Scripture, hence it is called harmony with the Spirit Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The reign title Kaihuang also matches the Kaihuang year in the Lingbao Scripture, which is why the text speaks of accord with the Spirit Emperor.

sentences.zh: 皇辟出者，皇，大也，辟，君也，大君出，蓋謂至尊受命出為天子也。

translations.literal: The great sovereign emerges—huang means great, pi means ruler; the great ruler emerges—presumably meaning the Supreme One received the mandate and emerged as Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The great sovereign comes forth—huang means great, pi means lord—and thus the great lord appears, meaning that His Majesty received the mandate and rose as Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 承元訖者，言承周天元終訖之運也。

translations.literal: He inherits the end of the Primordial Cycle means he inherited the course of the end of Zhou's primordial cycle.
translations.idiomatic: He succeeds when the Primordial Cycle ends means he inherited the fortune that closed Zhou's cosmic cycle.

sentences.zh: 道無為、治率者，治下脫一字，言大道無為，治定天下率從。

translations.literal: The Way is non-action; governance leads the masses—one character is missing below zhi; it means the Great Way is non-action, and having settled governance, the realm follows in accord.
translations.idiomatic: In The Way is effortless; rule guides all beneath Heaven, one character is missing after rule; the sense is that the Great Way acts without striving, and once order is settled the realm follows obediently.

sentences.zh: 被遂矩、戲作術者，矩，法也。

translations.literal: Clothed in Sui's square; playfully creating the art—ju is law.
translations.idiomatic: Invested with Sui's measure; devising the sacred arts in sport—here ju again means law.

sentences.zh: 昔遂皇握機矩，伏戲作八卦之術，言大隋被服三皇之法術也。

translations.literal: In antiquity Suí Huang grasped the pivot-square; Fuxi created the art of the Eight Trigrams—it means Great Sui received and adopted the laws and arts of the Three Sovereigns.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Suí Huang held the pivot of measure, and Fuxi devised the art of the Eight Trigrams—showing that Great Sui inherited the laws and arts of the Three Sovereigns.

sentences.zh: 遂皇機矩，語見易緯。

translations.literal: Suí Huang's pivot-square—the phrase appears in the Changes apocrypha.
translations.idiomatic: The phrase Suí Huang's pivot-square appears in the Changes apocrypha.

sentences.zh: 開皇色者，言開皇年易服色也。

translations.literal: Kaihuang color means in the Kaihuang era the official colors were changed.
translations.idiomatic: The hue of Kaihuang means that in the Kaihuang reign the court changed its ceremonial colors.

sentences.zh: 握神日者，握持羣神，明照如日也。

translations.literal: Grasping the divine sun means holding sway over all spirits, illuminating brilliantly like the sun.
translations.idiomatic: Holding fast to the divine sun means commanding all spirits and shining upon the world like the sun.

sentences.zh: 又開皇以來日漸長，亦其義。

translations.literal: Moreover since Kaihuang the days have gradually lengthened—this too is part of the meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Kaihuang era the days have grown longer—another sign contained in the same line.

sentences.zh: 投輔提者，言投授政事於輔佐，使之提挈也。

translations.literal: Entrusting to assistants to lead means delegating governance to assistants and having them take charge.
translations.idiomatic: Power is handed to ministers to bear up means that affairs of state are entrusted to counselors who lift and carry them.

sentences.zh: 象不絕者，法象不廢絕也。

translations.literal: The symbols are unbroken means the symbols of law were not abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: The patterns of rule never cease means that the institutions of law were not allowed to perish.

sentences.zh: 立皇後、翼不格者，格，至也，言本立太子以為皇家後嗣，而其輔翼之人不能至於善也。

translations.literal: Establishing the imperial heir; the winged helpers do not reach—ge means arrive; it means originally the crown prince was established as the imperial family's successor, yet those who should assist him could not reach goodness.
translations.idiomatic: An heir is installed; yet those who should support him fall short—ge means to attain—and refers to the crown prince being made imperial successor while his helpers failed to reach their duty.

sentences.zh: 道終始、德優劣者，言前東宮道終而德劣，今皇太子道始而德優也。

translations.literal: The Way ends and begins; virtue has superior and inferior means the former Eastern Palace's Way had ended and virtue was inferior; now the crown prince's Way is beginning and virtue is superior.
translations.idiomatic: One Way closes, another opens; virtue knows both decline and renewal means the former heir's path had ended in flawed virtue, whereas the present crown prince's path is just beginning in superior virtue.

sentences.zh: 帝任政、河曲出者，言皇帝親任政事，而邵州河濱得石圖也。

translations.literal: The emperor personally governs; the river bend produces a sign means the emperor personally undertook governance, and a stone chart was obtained on the riverbank at Shaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor himself takes up rule; a chart emerges from the river's bend refers to the emperor's personal involvement in government and the stone chart found on the Shaozhou riverbank.

sentences.zh: 協輔嬉、爛可述者，協，合也，嬉，興也，言羣臣合心輔佐，以興政治，爛然可紀述也。

translations.literal: Harmonious assistants rejoice; splendor worth recounting—xie means accord, xi means rise; it means the ministers united in heart to assist, to raise up governance, splendidly worth recording.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers unite in glad service; glory bright enough to be sung—xie means harmony, xi means flourishing—showing that the officials worked as one to raise up government in a splendor fit to be recorded.

sentences.zh: 所以於皇參持、帝通紀二篇陳大隋符命者，明皇道帝德，盡在隋也。

translations.literal: The reason for presenting Great Sui's mandate-tokens in the two scrolls Imperial Canopy Holder and Emperor Communication Record is to show that imperial Way and sovereign virtue reside entirely in Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant sets forth Great Sui's mandate in the Imperial Canopy Holder and Emperor Communication Record precisely to show that the imperial Way and sovereign virtue now dwell wholly in Sui.

sentences.zh: 上大悅，以劭為至誠，寵錫日隆。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased, regarded Shao as utterly sincere, and daily increased his favors and gifts.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted, judged Shao utterly sincere, and heaped ever greater favor upon him.

sentences.zh: 時有人於黃鳳泉浴，得二白石，頗有文理，遂附致其文以為字，復言有諸物象而上奏曰：「其大玉有日月星辰，八卦五岳，及二麟雙鳳，青龍朱雀，騶𩦢玄武，各當其方位。

translations.literal: At that time someone bathing at Huangfeng Spring obtained two white stones with distinct patterns; attaching the patterns as written characters, they further reported various images and submitted a memorial saying: On the larger jade are the sun, moon, stars, the Eight Trigrams, the Five Sacred Peaks, two qilin, paired phoenixes, the Azure Dragon, Vermilion Bird, zouyu, and Black Tortoise, each in its proper position.
translations.idiomatic: About that time a man bathing at Huangfeng Spring found two white stones marked with clear patterns. Treating the markings as written characters, he described the images they formed and memorialized the throne: The larger stone bears the sun, moon, and stars, the Eight Trigrams and Five Sacred Peaks, two qilin and paired phoenixes, the Azure Dragon, Vermilion Bird, zouyu, and Black Tortoise, each in its proper place.

sentences.zh: 又有五行、十日、十二辰之名，凡二十七字。

translations.literal: Also the names of the Five Phases, the Ten Days, and the Twelve Branches—in all twenty-seven characters.
translations.idiomatic: It also shows the names of the Five Phases, the ten heavenly stems, and the twelve earthly branches—twenty-seven characters in all.

sentences.zh: 又有『天門地戶人門鬼門閉』九字。

translations.literal: Also nine characters: Heaven Gate, Earth Gate, Human Gate, Ghost Gate, Closed.
translations.idiomatic: There are nine more characters: Heaven Gate, Earth Gate, Human Gate, Ghost Gate, Closed.

sentences.zh: 又有却非及二鳥，其鳥皆人面，則抱朴子所謂『千秋萬歲』也。

translations.literal: Also Quefei and two birds—all the birds have human faces, which is what the Baopuzi calls a thousand autumns, ten thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: There are also Quefei and two birds with human faces—the very Thousand Autumns, Ten Thousand Years described in the Baopuzi.

sentences.zh: 其小玉亦有五嶽、却非、虯、犀之象。

translations.literal: The smaller jade also has images of the Five Peaks, Quefei, dragons, and rhinoceroses.
translations.idiomatic: The smaller stone likewise bears the Five Peaks, Quefei, hornless dragons, and rhinoceroses.

sentences.zh: 二玉俱有仙人玉女乘雲控鶴之象。

translations.literal: Both jades have images of immortals and jade maidens riding clouds and controlling cranes.
translations.idiomatic: On both stones appear immortals and jade maidens riding clouds and guiding cranes.

sentences.zh: 別有異狀諸神，不可盡識，蓋是風伯、雨師、山精、海若之類。

translations.literal: Separately there are various gods of unusual form, impossible to identify fully—presumably the Wind Lord, Rain Master, mountain spirits, Sea Ruo, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: Other strange divine forms appear too numerous to name—likely the Wind Lord, Rain Master, mountain spirits, Sea Ruo, and their kind.

sentences.zh: 又有天皇大帝、皇帝及四帝坐，鉤陳、北斗、三公、天將軍、土司空、老人、天倉、南河、北河、五星、二十八宿，凡四十五官。

translations.literal: Also the Great Heavenly Emperor, the Emperor, and the Four Emperors seated; Gouchen, the Big Dipper, the Three Dukes, the Heavenly General, Tu Sikong, the Old Man, Heavenly Granary, South River, North River, the Five Stars, the Twenty-eight Lunar Mansions—in all forty-five officials.
translations.idiomatic: There are also the Great Heavenly Emperor, the Emperor, and the Four Emperors enthroned; Gouchen, the Northern Dipper, the Three Dukes, the Heavenly General, Tu Sikong, the Old Man, the Heavenly Granary, the South River, the North River, the Five Planets, and the Twenty-eight Mansions—forty-five celestial offices in all.

sentences.zh: 諸字本無行伍，然往往偶對。

translations.literal: The various characters originally had no order of ranks, yet often happened to pair in correspondence.
translations.idiomatic: The characters had no fixed arrangement, yet they often fell naturally into matching pairs.

sentences.zh: 於大玉則有皇帝姓名，並臨南面，與日字正鼎足。

translations.literal: On the larger jade are the emperor's name and surname, both facing south, forming a tripod with the character for sun.
translations.idiomatic: On the larger stone the emperor's personal and family names both face south, forming a tripod with the character for sun.

sentences.zh: 復有老人星，蓋明南面象日而長壽也。

translations.literal: Also the Old Man Star—presumably showing that facing south is like the sun and signifies long life.
translations.idiomatic: The Old Man Star appears as well, showing that to face south is to resemble the sun and to promise long life.

sentences.zh: 皇后二字在西，上有月形，蓋明象月也。

translations.literal: The two characters for empress are in the west, with a moon shape above—presumably showing the likeness to the moon.
translations.idiomatic: The two characters for empress stand in the west beneath the form of the moon, showing her likeness to the moon.

sentences.zh: 於次玉則皇帝名與九千字次比，兩『楊』字與『萬年』字次比，『隋』與『吉』字正並，蓋明長久吉慶也。

translations.literal: On the second jade the emperor's name is paired with the nine-thousand character; both characters Yang are paired with ten thousand years; Sui and auspicious are directly parallel—presumably showing enduring felicity.
translations.idiomatic: On the smaller stone the emperor's name stands beside the nine-thousand character; both instances of Yang pair with ten thousand years, and Sui aligns directly with auspicious—signs of enduring good fortune.

sentences.zh: 」劭復廻互其字，作詩二百八十篇奏之。

translations.literal: Shao again rearranged and interwove the characters, composed two hundred eighty poems, and submitted them.
translations.idiomatic: Shao then rearranged the characters in every possible combination, wrote two hundred and eighty poems, and presented them to the throne.

sentences.zh: 上以為誠，賜帛千匹。

translations.literal: The emperor regarded it as sincere and bestowed a thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted the work as genuine and rewarded him with a thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 劭於是採民間歌謠，引圖書讖緯，依約符命，捃摭佛經，撰為皇隋靈感誌，合三十卷，奏之。

translations.literal: Shao then gathered folk songs, cited charts, books, prophecies, and apocrypha, aligned them with mandate-tokens, collected passages from Buddhist sutras, and compiled the Imperial Sui Records of Spiritual Responsiveness in thirty scrolls, which he submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Shao thereupon collected popular ballads, drew upon charts, classics, prophecies, and apocrypha, matched them to signs of the mandate, gathered passages from Buddhist scriptures, and compiled the Imperial Sui Records of Spiritual Responsiveness in thirty scrolls, which he submitted to the throne.

sentences.zh: 上令宣示天下，劭集諸州朝集使，洗手焚香，閉目而讀之，曲折其聲，有如歌詠。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered it proclaimed throughout the realm. Shao assembled the provincial assembly envoys, washed hands and burned incense, closed their eyes and read it, modulating their voices as if singing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commanded that it be read aloud throughout the empire. Shao gathered the provincial tribute envoys, had them wash their hands, burn incense, close their eyes, and chant the text in a swaying, songlike voice.

sentences.zh: 經涉旬朔，徧而後罷。

translations.literal: After more than ten days and a new moon had passed, they had gone everywhere and then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The recitation continued for more than ten days, until every region had heard it, and only then ceased.

sentences.zh: 上益喜，賞賜優洽。

translations.literal: The emperor was all the more pleased and bestowed generous rewards.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's pleasure only grew, and his rewards were lavish.

sentences.zh: 仁壽中，文獻皇后崩，劭復上言曰：「佛說人應生天上，及上品上生無量壽國之時，天佛放大光明，以香花妓樂來迎之。

translations.literal: In the Renshou era, Empress Wenxian died. Shao again submitted a statement saying: The Buddha teaches that when a person is destined for rebirth in heaven, and especially for upper-grade upper rebirth in the Land of Infinite Life, the heavenly Buddhas radiate great light and come to welcome them with flowers, incense, and music.
translations.idiomatic: During the Renshou reign, Empress Wenxian passed away. Shao submitted another memorial: The Buddha teaches that when the worthy are reborn in heaven—and above all when they attain the highest grade of birth in the Land of Infinite Life—the Buddhas of heaven blaze with great light and come to receive them with incense, flowers, and celestial music.

sentences.zh: 如來以明星出時入涅槃。

translations.literal: The Tathagata entered nirvana at the hour when the morning star appeared.
translations.idiomatic: The Tathagata entered nirvana at the hour when the morning star rose.

sentences.zh: 伏惟大行皇后聖德仁慈，福善禎符，備諸祕記，皆云是妙善菩薩。

translations.literal: I humbly consider that the late empress's sacred virtue was benevolent; blessed with fortune and auspicious signs, all secret records say she was the Bodhisattva Miaoshan.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly reflect that the late empress possessed sacred and merciful virtue, blessed with fortune and prophetic warrant; every secret scripture declares her to have been the Bodhisattva Miaoshan.

sentences.zh: 臣謹案：八月二十二日，仁壽宮內再雨金銀之花。

translations.literal: Your servant respectfully submits: On the twenty-second day of the eighth month, flowers of gold and silver rained again within Renshou Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant respectfully submits that on the twenty-second day of the eighth month, flowers of gold and silver fell once more inside Renshou Palace.

sentences.zh: 二十三日，大寶殿後夜有神光。

translations.literal: On the twenty-third, at night behind the Hall of Great Treasure there was divine light.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-third, a supernatural light appeared at night behind the Hall of Great Treasure.

sentences.zh: 二十四日卯時，永安宮北有自然種種音樂，震滿虛空。

translations.literal: On the twenty-fourth at the hour of mao, north of Yong'an Palace there was naturally all manner of music, reverberating and filling the empty sky.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-fourth at dawn, north of Yong'an Palace, music of every kind arose spontaneously, thundering through the empty heavens.

sentences.zh: 至夜五更中，奄然如寐，便即升遐，與經文所說，事皆符驗。

translations.literal: Reaching the fifth watch of the night, suddenly as if falling asleep, she at once ascended to the far realm; with what the scriptures described, the events all matched and were verified.
translations.idiomatic: By the fifth watch of the night she suddenly sank as if into sleep and at once departed this life—everything accorded with the scriptures, and each sign was fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 臣又以愚意思之，皇后遷化，不在仁壽、大興宮者，蓋避至尊常居正處也。

translations.literal: Your servant further considers in my foolish mind that the empress's passing, not at Renshou or Daxing Palace, was probably to avoid the sovereign's regular dwelling in the principal residence.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant further reflects in my simple-minded way that the empress did not pass away at Renshou or Daxing Palace because she wished to avoid the sovereign's own principal residence.

sentences.zh: 在永安宮者，象京師之永安門，平生所出入也。

translations.literal: That she was at Yong'an Palace symbolizes Yong'an Gate of the capital—the gate through which she passed in and out throughout her life.
translations.idiomatic: Her presence at Yong'an Palace symbolized Yong'an Gate of the capital, the gate through which she had passed all her life.

sentences.zh: 后升遐後二日，苑內夜有鍾聲三百餘處，此則生天之應顯然也。

translations.literal: Two days after the empress ascended, at night bell sounds were heard in more than three hundred places within the park—this was clearly the response of rebirth in heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Two nights after the empress's death, bell sounds were heard at more than three hundred places in the palace grounds—a clear sign that she had been reborn in heaven.

sentences.zh: 」上覽而且悲且喜。

translations.literal: The emperor read it and was both grieved and pleased.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor read the memorial, he was at once sorrowful and glad.

sentences.zh: 時蜀王秀以罪廢，上顧謂劭曰：「嗟乎！

translations.literal: At that time Prince of Shu Xiu was deposed for his crimes; the emperor turned and said to Shao: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: At that time Prince Xiu of Shu had been stripped of his title for his crimes, and the emperor turned to Shao and said, "Alas!

sentences.zh: 吾有五子，三子不才。

translations.literal: I have five sons, and three are without talent.
translations.idiomatic: I have five sons, and three of them are worthless."

sentences.zh: 」劭進曰：「自古聖帝明王，皆不能移不肖之子。

translations.literal: Shao stepped forward and said: Since antiquity even sage emperors and enlightened kings have been unable to change unworthy sons.
translations.idiomatic: Shao stepped forward and said, "Since antiquity even sage emperors and enlightened kings have been unable to reform unworthy sons.

sentences.zh: 黃帝有二十五子，同姓者二，餘各異德。

translations.literal: The Yellow Emperor had twenty-five sons; only two shared his surname, the rest each had different virtues.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Emperor had twenty-five sons, but only two bore his surname; the rest each possessed a different virtue.

sentences.zh: 堯十子，舜九子，皆不肖。

translations.literal: Yao had ten sons and Shun nine sons, all unworthy.
translations.idiomatic: Yao had ten sons and Shun nine sons, and all were unworthy.

sentences.zh: 夏有五觀，周有三監。

translations.literal: Xia had the Five Guan; Zhou had the Three Overseers.
translations.idiomatic: Xia had the Five Guan, and Zhou had the Three Overseers."

sentences.zh: 」上然其言。

translations.literal: The emperor agreed with his words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted what he said.

sentences.zh: 其後上夢欲上高山而不能得，崔彭捧脚，李盛扶肘得上，因謂彭曰：「死生當與爾俱。

translations.literal: Later the emperor dreamed of wishing to climb a high mountain but could not; Cui Peng held his feet and Li Sheng supported his elbow until he got up, whereupon he said to Peng: In life and death I shall be with you.
translations.idiomatic: Later the emperor dreamed that he wished to climb a high mountain but could not; Cui Peng held his feet and Li Sheng supported his arms until he reached the summit, and he then said to Peng, "In life and death I shall be with you.

sentences.zh: 」劭曰：「此夢大吉。

translations.literal: Shao said: This dream is greatly auspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Shao said, "This dream is exceedingly auspicious.

sentences.zh: 上高山者，明高崇大安，永如山也。

translations.literal: Climbing a high mountain signifies lofty eminence, great peace, enduring as a mountain.
translations.idiomatic: To climb a high mountain means lofty stature, great peace, and endurance firm as a mountain.

sentences.zh: 彭猶彭祖，李猶李老，二人扶侍，實為長壽之徵。

translations.literal: Peng is like Peng Zu, Li is like Old Master Li; that two men supported and served him is truly a sign of long life.
translations.idiomatic: Peng recalls Peng Zu, and Li recalls Old Master Li; that two such men supported him is truly a sign of long life."

sentences.zh: 」上聞之，喜見容色。

translations.literal: The emperor heard this and joy showed on his face.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard this, delight showed plainly on his face.

sentences.zh: 其年，上崩。

translations.literal: That year the emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: That same year the emperor died.

sentences.zh: 未幾，崔彭亦卒。

translations.literal: Before long Cui Peng also died.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Cui Peng died as well.

sentences.zh: 煬帝嗣位，漢王諒作亂，帝不忍加誅。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne; Prince of Han Liang rebelled, but the emperor could not bear to put him to death.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, Prince Liang of Han rose in rebellion, but the emperor could not bring himself to execute him.

sentences.zh: 劭上書曰：「臣聞黃帝滅炎，蓋云母弟，周公誅管，信亦天倫。

translations.literal: Shao submitted a memorial saying: Your servant has heard that when the Yellow Emperor destroyed Yan, it is said he was a younger uterine brother; when the Duke of Zhou executed Guan, that too was family kin.
translations.idiomatic: Shao submitted a memorial saying, "Your servant has heard that when the Yellow Emperor destroyed Yan, it is said the man was his younger uterine brother, and when the Duke of Zhou executed Guan, that too was a matter of blood kinship.

sentences.zh: 叔向戮叔魚，仲尼謂之遺直，石碏殺石厚，丘明以為大義。

translations.literal: Shu Xiang executed Shu Yu—Confucius called this inherited integrity; Shi Que killed Shi Hou—Qiu Ming considered it great righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Shu Xiang put Shu Yu to death, and Confucius called this the uprightness handed down in his family; Shi Que killed Shi Hou, and Zuo Qiuming judged it a deed of great righteousness.

sentences.zh: 此皆經籍明文，帝王常法。

translations.literal: These are all plain statements in the classics—the standard method of emperors and kings.
translations.idiomatic: These are all explicit passages in the classics—the constant practice of emperors and kings.

sentences.zh: 今陛下置此逆賊，度越前聖，含弘寬大，未有以謝天下。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty has spared this rebel traitor, surpassing the former sages in magnanimity and forbearance—yet there is no way to answer the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty has left this rebel unpunished, surpassing the sages of old in clemency and breadth of mind, yet offering the realm no sufficient account.

sentences.zh: 謹案賊諒毒被生民者也。

translations.literal: Your servant respectfully submits that the rebel Liang poisoned and afflicted the common people.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant respectfully submits that the rebel Liang spread poison and harm among the people.

sentences.zh: 是知古者同德則同姓，異德則異姓，故黃帝有二十五子，其得姓者十有四人，唯青陽、夷鼓，與黃帝同為姬姓。

translations.literal: From this we know that in antiquity those of the same virtue shared a surname, those of different virtue had different surnames; thus of the Yellow Emperor's twenty-five sons, fourteen received surnames, and only Qingyang and Yigu shared the Ji surname with the Yellow Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: From this we know that in antiquity those of the same virtue shared a surname and those of different virtue took different surnames; of the Yellow Emperor's twenty-five sons, fourteen received surnames, and only Qingyang and Yigu shared the Ji surname with the Yellow Emperor.

sentences.zh: 諒既自絕，請改其氏。

translations.literal: Since Liang has cut himself off, I request that his clan name be changed.
translations.idiomatic: Since Liang has cut himself off from his house, I ask that his surname be changed."

sentences.zh: 」劭以此求媚，帝依違不從。

translations.literal: Shao sought favor in this way; the emperor wavered but did not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Shao was currying favor in this way, but the emperor hesitated and did not follow his advice.

sentences.zh: 遷祕書少監，數載，卒官。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Secretariat; after several years he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Secretariat and, after several years, died in that post.

sentences.zh: 劭在著作，將二十年，專典國史，撰隋書八十卷。

translations.literal: Shao served in the Writing Office for nearly twenty years, chiefly in charge of the national history, and compiled eighty volumes of the Book of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Shao served in the Writing Office for nearly twenty years, chiefly overseeing the national history, and compiled eighty volumes of the Book of Sui.

sentences.zh: 多錄口勑，又採迂怪不經之語及委巷之言，以類相從，為其題目，辭義繁雜，無足稱者，遂使隋代文武名臣列將善惡之迹，堙沒無聞。

translations.literal: He recorded many oral edicts and collected absurd, unorthodox sayings and alley gossip, arranging them by category under various titles—verbose and muddled, unworthy of note—so that the deeds good and ill of Sui's civil and military ministers and generals were buried in obscurity.
translations.idiomatic: He copied down many oral edicts and gathered outlandish, unorthodox tales and back-alley gossip, sorting them by category under various titles; the language was tangled and worthless, so that the deeds, good and ill, of Sui's civil and military ministers and generals were buried without a hearing.

sentences.zh: 初撰齊誌，為編年體，二十卷，復為齊書紀傳一百卷，及平賊記三卷。

translations.literal: He first compiled the Chronicle of Qi in annalistic form, twenty volumes; he also compiled a Qi history in biographical annals, one hundred volumes, plus three volumes of the Record of Pacifying Rebels.
translations.idiomatic: He first compiled the Chronicle of Qi in annalistic form in twenty volumes, then a Qi history in annal-biography form in one hundred volumes, as well as three volumes of the Record of Pacifying Rebels.

sentences.zh: 或文詞鄙野，或不軌不物，駭人視聽，大為有識所嗤鄙。

translations.literal: Some passages were crude in language, some irregular and bizarre, shocking to hear and see, and widely mocked by the discerning.
translations.idiomatic: Some of his writing was coarse and vulgar, some of it irregular and outlandish, shocking to eye and ear, and widely scorned by men of discernment.

sentences.zh: 然其採擿經史謬誤，為讀書記三十卷，時人服其精博。

translations.literal: Yet in collecting and correcting errors in the classics and histories he compiled thirty volumes of Reading Notes, and contemporaries admired his precision and breadth.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in gathering and correcting errors in the classics and histories he compiled thirty volumes of Reading Notes, and men of his time admired his precision and breadth.

sentences.zh: 爰自志學，暨乎暮齒，篤好經史，遺落世事。

translations.literal: From the age of vigorous learning to the teeth of old age he devoted himself to the classics and histories and neglected worldly affairs.
translations.idiomatic: From youth to old age he devoted himself tirelessly to the classics and histories and paid little heed to worldly affairs.

sentences.zh: 用思既專，性頗怳忽，每至對食，閉目凝思，盤中之肉，輒為僕從所噉。

translations.literal: His concentration was so intense and his nature so absent-minded that whenever he sat down to eat, he would close his eyes and ponder; the meat on his plate would then be eaten by his attendants.
translations.idiomatic: His mind was so wholly absorbed and his temperament so absent that whenever he sat down to eat, he would close his eyes in deep thought, and the meat on his plate would be eaten by his attendants.

sentences.zh: 劭弗之覺，唯責肉少，數罰厨人。

translations.literal: Shao never noticed, only blamed the paucity of meat and repeatedly punished the kitchen staff.
translations.idiomatic: Shao never noticed, but only complained that there was too little meat and repeatedly punished the cooks.

sentences.zh: 厨人以情白劭，劭依前閉目，伺而獲之，厨人方免笞辱。

translations.literal: The kitchen staff explained the truth to Shao; Shao as before closed his eyes and waited until he caught them in the act, and only then were the kitchen staff spared beating.
translations.idiomatic: The cooks told him what was happening; Shao closed his eyes as before, waited, and caught them in the act, and only then were the cooks spared a beating.

sentences.zh: 其專固如此。

translations.literal: Such was the fixity of his concentration.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the obstinate fixity of his concentration.

sentences.zh: 袁充袁充字德符，本陳郡陽夏人也。

translations.literal: Yuan Chong—Yuan Chong's style name was Defu, and he was originally a man of Yangxia in Chen Commandery.
