translations.idiomatic: Yuan Chong, styled Defu, was originally a native of Yangxia in Chen Commandery.

sentences.zh: 其後寓居丹陽。

translations.literal: Later he took up residence in Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Later he settled in Danyang.

sentences.zh: 祖昂，父君正，俱為梁侍中。

translations.literal: His grandfather Ang and his father Junzheng both served Liang as Attendants-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Ang and his father Junzheng had both served as Liang Attendants-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 充少警悟，年十餘歲，其父黨至門，時冬初，充尚衣葛衫。

translations.literal: Chong as a youth was quick-witted; when he was just over ten, a friend of his father's came to the door—it was early winter and Chong was still wearing a hemp-cloth shirt.
translations.idiomatic: Chong was quick-witted from boyhood; when he was little more than ten, a friend of his father's came to visit. It was early winter, yet Chong was still wearing a thin hemp shirt.

sentences.zh: 客戲充曰：「袁郎子絺兮𥿭兮，淒其以風。

translations.literal: The guest teased Chong, saying: Master Yuan, fine and coarse linen—how bleak with the wind.
translations.idiomatic: The guest teased him, quoting the Odes: "Young Master Yuan, in fine and coarse linen—how chill the wind blows."

sentences.zh: 」充應聲答曰：「唯絺與𥿭，服之無斁。

translations.literal: Chong answered on the spot: Only fine and coarse linen—to wear them without satiety.
translations.idiomatic: Chong answered at once, "Only fine and coarse linen—to wear them and never grow weary."

sentences.zh: 」以是大見嗟賞。

translations.literal: For this he won great admiration.
translations.idiomatic: For this he won great admiration.

sentences.zh: 仕陳，年十七，為秘書郎。

translations.literal: He entered Chen service; at seventeen he became Secretary Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He entered Chen service and at seventeen was appointed Secretary Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 歷太子舍人、晉安王文學、吏部侍郎、散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He served successively as Crown Prince Attendant, Literary Companion to Prince of Jin'an, Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, and Regular Attendant of the Cavalry-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession as Crown Prince Attendant, Literary Companion to the Prince of Jin'an, Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, and Regular Attendant of the Cavalry-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 及陳滅歸國，歷蒙、鄜二州司馬。

translations.literal: When Chen fell and he returned to the realm, he served successively as Regional Administrator of Meng and Fu provinces.
translations.idiomatic: After Chen fell and he returned to the new dynasty, he served successively as Regional Administrator in Meng and Fu provinces.

sentences.zh: 充性好道術，頗解占候，由是領太史令。

translations.literal: Chong was fond of Daoist arts and understood divination and portents well; for this reason he was appointed Director of the Imperial Observatory.
translations.idiomatic: Chong loved the arts of the Way and was well versed in divination and celestial portents; for this reason he was appointed Director of the Imperial Observatory.

sentences.zh: 時上將廢皇太子，正窮治東宮官屬，充見上雅信符應，因希旨進曰：「比觀玄象，皇太子當廢。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor was about to depose the crown prince and was thoroughly investigating the Eastern Palace staff; Chong saw that the emperor trusted omens and portents, and seeking to please him stepped forward saying: Recently observing the celestial signs, the crown prince ought to be deposed.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the emperor was about to depose the crown prince and was rigorously investigating the officials of the Eastern Palace; seeing that the emperor placed great faith in omens and portents, Chong sought to please him and said, "In recent observations of the celestial signs, the crown prince should be deposed.

sentences.zh: 」上然之。

translations.literal: The emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted this."

sentences.zh: 充復表奏，隋興已後，日影漸長，曰：「開皇元年，冬至日影一丈二尺七寸二分，自爾漸短。

translations.literal: Chong submitted another memorial, noting that since Sui's rise the noon shadow had gradually lengthened, saying: In the first year of Kaihuang, the winter solstice shadow was one zhang, two chi, seven cun, and two fen; thereafter it gradually shortened.
translations.idiomatic: Chong submitted another memorial stating that since the rise of Sui the solar shadow had gradually lengthened, saying, "In the first year of Kaihuang the winter-solstice shadow was one zhang, two chi, seven cun, and two fen; from then on it gradually shortened.

sentences.zh: 至十七年，冬至影一丈二尺六寸三分。

translations.literal: By the seventeenth year the winter solstice shadow was one zhang, two chi, six cun, and three fen.
translations.idiomatic: By the seventeenth year the winter-solstice shadow was one zhang, two chi, six cun, and three fen.

sentences.zh: 四年冬至，在洛陽測影，一丈二尺八寸八分。

translations.literal: On the winter solstice of the fourth year, measuring the shadow at Luoyang, it was one zhang, two chi, eight cun, and eight fen.
translations.idiomatic: On the winter solstice of the fourth year, when the shadow was measured at Luoyang, it was one zhang, two chi, eight cun, and eight fen.

sentences.zh: 二年，夏至影一尺四寸八分，自爾漸短。

translations.literal: In the second year the summer solstice shadow was one chi, four cun, and eight fen; thereafter it gradually shortened.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year the summer-solstice shadow was one chi, four cun, and eight fen; from then on it gradually shortened.

sentences.zh: 至十六年，夏至影一尺四寸五分。

translations.literal: By the sixteenth year the summer solstice shadow was one chi, four cun, and five fen.
translations.idiomatic: By the sixteenth year the summer-solstice shadow was one chi, four cun, and five fen.

sentences.zh: 周官以土圭之法正日影，日至之影尺有五寸。

translations.literal: The Offices of Zhou uses the earth-gnomon method to determine the solar shadow; the shadow at solstice is one chi and five cun.
translations.idiomatic: The Offices of Zhou uses the earth-gnomon method to fix the solar shadow; at the solstice the shadow should be one chi and five cun.

sentences.zh: 鄭玄云：『冬至之影一丈三尺。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan said: The winter solstice shadow is one zhang and three chi.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan said, "The winter-solstice shadow is one zhang and three chi.

sentences.zh: 』今十六年夏至之影，短於舊影五分，十七年冬至之影，短於舊影三寸七分。

translations.literal: The sixteenth-year summer solstice shadow is five fen shorter than the old shadow; the seventeenth-year winter solstice shadow is three cun and seven fen shorter than the old shadow.
translations.idiomatic: Now the summer-solstice shadow of the sixteenth year is five fen shorter than the old standard, and the winter-solstice shadow of the seventeenth year is three cun and seven fen shorter than the old standard.

sentences.zh: 日去極近則影短而日長，去極遠則影長而日短，行內道則去極近，外道則去極遠。

translations.literal: When the sun is near the pole the shadow is short and the day long; when far from the pole the shadow is long and the day short; traveling the inner path brings it near the pole, the outer path far from it.
translations.idiomatic: When the sun is near the pole the shadow is short and the day is long; when it is far from the pole the shadow is long and the day is short; on the inner path it draws near the pole, and on the outer path it draws far from it.

sentences.zh: 堯典云：『日短星昴，以正仲冬。

translations.literal: The Canon of Yao says: The day is short and the star Mao culminates at dusk—to fix midwinter.
translations.idiomatic: The Canon of Yao says, "The days are short and the star Mao culminates at dusk—thus midwinter is fixed.

sentences.zh: 』據昴星昏中，則知堯時仲冬，日在須女十度。

translations.literal: From Mao's culmination at dusk we know that at Yao's midwinter the sun was at the tenth degree of Xu-Nü.
translations.idiomatic: From the dusk culmination of Mao we know that at Yao's midwinter the sun stood at the tenth degree of Maid.

sentences.zh: 以曆數推之，開皇已來冬至，日在斗十一度，與唐堯之代去極並近。

translations.literal: Calculating by calendrical reckoning, from Kaihuang onward at winter solstice the sun has been at the eleventh degree of Dipper—like the age of Tang Yao, equally near the pole.
translations.idiomatic: By calendrical calculation, from Kaihuang onward the sun at winter solstice has stood at the eleventh degree of Dipper—like the age of Tang Yao, equally near the pole.

sentences.zh: 謹案春秋元命包云：『日月出內道，琁璣得常，天帝崇靈，聖王祖功。

translations.literal: Your servant respectfully cites the Spring and Autumn Yuanming Bao: Sun and moon travel the inner path; the jade pivots hold their course; the Heavenly Emperor exalts spirit; sage kings honor ancestral merit.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant respectfully cites the Spring and Autumn Yuanming Bao: "When sun and moon emerge on the inner path, the jade pivots keep their regular course, the Heavenly Emperor exalts the numinous, and sage kings honor the merit of their ancestors.

sentences.zh: 』京房別對曰：『太平日行上道，升平行次道，霸世行下道。

translations.literal: Jing Fang's separate response says: In Great Peace the sun travels the upper path; in ascending peace the middle path; in hegemonic ages the lower path.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's separate response says, "In an age of Great Peace the sun travels the upper path; in an age of ascending peace the middle path; in an age of hegemony the lower path.

sentences.zh: 』伏惟大隋啟運，上感乾元，影短日長，振古未之有也。

translations.literal: Great Sui has opened its destiny, moved by the primordial qi of Heaven—short shadows and long days, unprecedented since antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Great Sui has opened its destiny, stirred by the primordial power of Heaven—short shadows and long days, a thing unheard of since antiquity."

sentences.zh: 」上大悅，告天下。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and proclaimed it to the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased and proclaimed this to the empire.

sentences.zh: 將作役功，因加程課，丁匠苦之。

translations.literal: When construction conscript labor intensified work quotas, the corvée artisans suffered.
translations.idiomatic: When the Directorate of Palace Construction increased labor quotas on the conscripted craftsmen, the corvée workers were driven to misery.

sentences.zh: 仁壽初，充言上本命與陰陽律呂合者六十餘條而奏之，因上表曰：「皇帝載誕之初，非止神光瑞氣，嘉祥應感，至於本命行年，生月生日，並與天地日月、陰陽律呂運轉相符，表裏合會。

translations.literal: Early in Renshou, Chong reported more than sixty correspondences between the emperor's natal destiny and the yin-yang pitch-pipes, and submitted a memorial saying: From the moment of the emperor's birth, not only divine light and auspicious qi, lucky omens and responsive portents—down to natal year, birth month, and birth day—all accord with the revolutions of heaven and earth, sun and moon, yin and yang and the pitch-pipes, inner and outer in perfect harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Renshou era, Chong reported more than sixty correspondences between the emperor's natal destiny and the yin-yang pitch-pipes, and submitted a memorial saying, "From the moment of the emperor's birth there were not only divine light and auspicious qi, felicitous omens and responsive signs, but even his natal year, birth month, and birth day all matched the revolutions of heaven and earth, sun and moon, yin and yang, and the pitch-pipes, inner and outer in perfect accord.

sentences.zh: 此誕聖之異，寶曆之元。

translations.literal: This is the wonder of a sage's birth, the origin of an imperial era.
translations.idiomatic: This is the marvel of a sage's birth and the foundation of an imperial age.

sentences.zh: 今與物更新，改年仁壽，歲月日子，還共誕聖之時並同，明合天地之心，得仁壽之理。

translations.literal: Now as all things renew and the era is changed to Renshou, year, month, day, and hour again coincide with the time of the sage's birth—clearly in accord with Heaven and Earth's intent, attaining the principle of benevolence and longevity.
translations.idiomatic: Now, as all things are renewed and the reign title is changed to Renshou, the year, month, day, and hour again coincide with the time of the sage's birth, clearly matching the mind of Heaven and Earth and attaining the principle of benevolence and long life.

sentences.zh: 故知洪基長算，永永無窮。

translations.literal: Thus we know the great foundation stands for a long span, forever without end.
translations.idiomatic: Thus we know that the great foundation will endure for a long span, forever without end."

sentences.zh: 」上大悅，賞賜優崇，儕輩莫之比。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased; rewards and honors were generous beyond any of his peers.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased, and the rewards and honors he received were beyond comparison among his peers.

sentences.zh: 仁壽四年甲子歲，煬帝初即位，充及太史丞高智寶奏言：「去歲冬至，日影逾長，今歲皇帝即位，與堯受命年合。

translations.literal: In the jiazi year, the fourth year of Renshou, when Emperor Yang first acceded, Chong and Observatory Vice Director Gao Zhibao submitted: Last winter solstice the solar shadow grew longer; this year the emperor acceded, matching the year of Yao's receiving the mandate.
translations.idiomatic: In the jiazi year of the fourth year of Renshou, when Emperor Yang first took the throne, Chong and Observatory Vice Director Gao Zhibao submitted a memorial saying, "Last winter solstice the solar shadow grew longer, and this year, when the emperor acceded, matches the year in which Yao received the mandate.

sentences.zh: 昔唐堯受命四十九年，到上元第一紀甲子，天正十一月庚戌冬至，陛下即位，其年即當上元第一紀甲子，天正十一月庚戌冬至，正與唐堯同。

translations.literal: Formerly Tang Yao received the mandate in the forty-ninth year; at the first jiazi of the first Upper Origin cycle, heavenly first month, gengxu day at winter solstice—Your Majesty acceded in that very year, which is exactly the first jiazi of the first Upper Origin cycle, heavenly first month, gengxu day at winter solstice—precisely the same as Tang Yao.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Tang Yao received the mandate in his forty-ninth year; at the first jiazi of the first Upper Origin cycle, in the heavenly first month on the gengxu day at winter solstice—Your Majesty acceded in that very year, which is exactly the first jiazi of the first Upper Origin cycle, in the heavenly first month on the gengxu day at winter solstice, precisely the same as Tang Yao.

sentences.zh: 自放勳以來，凡經八上元，其間緜代，未有仁壽甲子之合。

translations.literal: Since Fang Xun, eight Upper Origins have passed; through long ages none has matched the Renshou jiazi alignment.
translations.idiomatic: Since the time of Fangxun, eight Upper Origins have passed, and through all the long ages none has matched the conjunction of Renshou and jiazi.

sentences.zh: 謹案：第一紀甲子，太一在一宮，天目居武德，陰陽曆數並得符同。

translations.literal: Your servant respectfully submits: in the first cycle's jiazi, Great One is in the first palace, Celestial Eye dwells in Wude—yin-yang and calendrical numbers all correspond.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant respectfully submits that in the first cycle's jiazi, Great One stands in the first palace and Celestial Eye dwells in Wude, and the numbers of yin and yang and of the calendar all correspond.

sentences.zh: 唐堯丙辰生，丙子年受命，止合三五，未若己丑甲子，支干並當六合。

translations.literal: Tang Yao was born in bingchen, received the mandate in bingzi year—matching only three-five; not like jichou and jiazi, both stem-branch pairs perfectly matching the six harmonies.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Yao was born in a bingchen year and received the mandate in a bingzi year, matching only the three-five pattern, unlike jichou and jiazi, whose stem-branch combinations both fall perfectly within the six harmonies.

sentences.zh: 允一元三統之期，合五紀九章之會，共帝堯同其數，與皇唐比其蹤。

translations.literal: Fulfilling the term of one origin and three sequences, matching the convergence of five eras and nine chapters—sharing Emperor Yao's numbers, comparable to august Tang's traces.
translations.idiomatic: This fulfills the term of one origin and three sequences and matches the convergence of five eras and nine chapters, sharing Emperor Yao's numbers and comparable to the august traces of Tang.

sentences.zh: 信所謂皇哉唐哉，唐哉皇哉者矣。

translations.literal: Truly what is meant by How glorious is Tang! How glorious is Tang!
translations.idiomatic: Truly this is what is meant by "How glorious is Tang! How glorious is Tang!"

sentences.zh: 」仍諷齊王暕率百官拜表奉賀。

translations.literal: He also prompted Prince of Qi Yang to lead the hundred officials in submitting a congratulatory memorial.
translations.idiomatic: He also prompted Prince Yang of Qi to lead the hundred officials in submitting a congratulatory memorial.

sentences.zh: 其後熒惑守太微者數旬，于時繕治宮室，征役繁重，充上表稱「陛下修德，熒惑退舍」。

translations.literal: Thereafter Mars stayed in Taiwei for several tens of days; at the time palace construction was underway and conscription heavy; Chong submitted a memorial saying Your Majesty cultivates virtue, and Mars has withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Mars lingered in Taiwei for several tens of days; at the time palace construction was underway and conscription was heavy, yet Chong submitted a memorial saying, "Your Majesty cultivates virtue, and Mars has withdrawn from its station."

sentences.zh: 百僚畢賀。

translations.literal: The hundred officials all congratulated.
translations.idiomatic: All the officials congratulated him.

sentences.zh: 帝大喜，前後賞賜將萬計。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased; rewards before and after totaled nearly ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased, and rewards given before and after totaled nearly ten thousand items.

sentences.zh: 時軍國多務，充候帝意欲有所為，便奏稱天文見象，須有改作，以是取媚於上。

translations.literal: At that time military and state affairs were numerous; Chong watched the emperor's intentions and whenever he wished to act, would submit that celestial signs appeared requiring changes—thus currying favor with the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: At that time military and state affairs were pressing; Chong watched the emperor's intentions, and whenever the emperor wished to act, he would submit that celestial signs required some change—thus currying favor with the throne.

sentences.zh: 大業六年，遷內史舍人。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Daye he was promoted to Drafter of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Daye he was promoted to Drafter of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 從征遼東，拜朝請大夫、秘書少監。

translations.literal: On the Liaodong campaign he was appointed Grand Master for Closing Audience and Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On the campaign against Liaodong he was appointed Grand Master for Closing Audience and Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 其後天下亂，帝初罹雁門之厄，又盜賊益起，帝心不自安。

translations.literal: Thereafter the realm fell into disorder; the emperor first suffered the crisis at Yanmen, and bandits rose in increasing numbers; the emperor's heart was ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the empire fell into disorder; the emperor first suffered the crisis at Yanmen, and bandits rose in ever greater numbers, so that his mind was no longer at ease.

sentences.zh: 充復假託天文，上表陳嘉瑞，以媚於上曰：

translations.literal: Chong again feigned astronomical signs and submitted a memorial presenting auspicious portents to flatter the sovereign, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Chong again fabricated celestial signs and submitted a memorial presenting auspicious portents to flatter the emperor, saying:

sentences.zh: :臣聞皇天輔德，皇天福謙，七政斯齊，三辰告應。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that August Heaven aids the virtuous and blesses the humble; the seven regulators are aligned, the three luminaries proclaim their response.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has heard that August Heaven aids the virtuous and blesses the humble, that the seven regulators stand in harmony and the three luminaries proclaim their response.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下握錄圖而馭黔首，提萬善而化八紘，以百姓為心，匪以一人受慶，先天罔違所欲，後天必奉其時。

translations.literal: Your Majesty grasps the cosmic chart and governs the black-haired people, uplifts all virtue and transforms the eight directions—taking the common people as his heart, not seeking fortune for himself alone; what is desired before Heaven is never thwarted, what follows Heaven is always timely.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty grasps the register of fate and governs the black-haired people, uplifts all goodness and transforms the eight directions, taking the common people to heart rather than seeking fortune for himself alone; what is desired beforehand is never thwarted by Heaven, and what comes afterward is always offered up in season.

sentences.zh: 是以初膺寶曆，正當上元之紀，乾之初九，又與天命符會。

translations.literal: Thus upon first receiving the imperial succession, it fell exactly in the cycle of the Upper Origin, Qian's initial nine—again matching Heaven's mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Thus, when you first received the imperial succession, it fell exactly in the cycle of the Upper Origin and in Qian's initial nine line, again matching Heaven's mandate.

sentences.zh: 斯則聖人冥契，故能動合天經。

translations.literal: This is the sage's hidden accord—therefore his actions match Heaven's constant.
translations.idiomatic: This is the sage's secret accord with Heaven, and therefore his actions match Heaven's constant way.

sentences.zh: 謹按去年已來，玄象星瑞，毫釐無爽，謹錄尤異，上天降祥、破突厥等狀七事。

translations.literal: Your servant respectfully submits that since last year celestial signs and stellar portents have not deviated by a hair's breadth; your servant respectfully records the most extraordinary, seven items including Heaven sending blessings and breaking the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant respectfully submits that since last year the celestial signs and stellar portents have not deviated by a hair's breadth; your servant respectfully records the most extraordinary among them, seven matters including Heaven sending down blessings and the destruction of the Turks.

sentences.zh: :其一，去八月二十八日夜，大流星如斗，出王良北，正落突厥營，聲如崩牆。

translations.literal: First: on the night of the twenty-eighth of the eighth month last year, a great meteor the size of a dipper emerged north of Wang Liang and fell directly on the Turk camp, with a sound like a collapsing wall.
translations.idiomatic: First: on the night of the twenty-eighth of the eighth month last year, a great meteor as large as the Dipper emerged north of Wang Liang and fell directly on the Turk camp, with a sound like a collapsing wall.

sentences.zh: 其二，八月二十九日夜，復有大流星如斗，出羽林，向北流，正當北方。

translations.literal: Second: on the night of the twenty-ninth of the eighth month, again a great meteor like a dipper emerged from Yulin, flowed northward, directly toward the north.
translations.idiomatic: Second: on the night of the twenty-ninth of the eighth month, again a great meteor as large as the Dipper emerged from Yulin, flowed northward, and headed straight toward the north.

sentences.zh: 依占，頻二夜流星墜賊所，賊必敗散。

translations.literal: According to divination, meteors falling on the rebels' position for two nights in succession—the rebels will surely be defeated and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: According to divination, when meteors fall on the enemy's position on two successive nights, the enemy will surely be defeated and scattered.

sentences.zh: 其三，九月四日夜，頻有兩星大如斗，出北斗魁，向東北流。

translations.literal: Third: on the night of the fourth of the ninth month, repeatedly two stars as large as a dipper emerged from the Dipper's handle and flowed northeast.
translations.idiomatic: Third: on the night of the fourth of the ninth month, two stars as large as the Dipper repeatedly emerged from the handle of the Northern Dipper and flowed toward the northeast.

sentences.zh: 依占，北斗主殺伐，賊必敗。

translations.literal: According to divination, the Northern Dipper governs killing and punishment—the rebels will surely be defeated.
translations.idiomatic: According to divination, the Northern Dipper governs killing and punishment, so the enemy will surely be defeated.

sentences.zh: 其四，歲星主福德，頻行京、都二處分野。

translations.literal: Fourth: Jupiter governs fortune and virtue, repeatedly traversing the territorial allotments of Jing and Du.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth: Jupiter governs fortune and virtue and has repeatedly passed through the territorial allotments of Jing and Du.

sentences.zh: 依占，國家之福。

translations.literal: According to divination, this is the nation's blessing.
translations.idiomatic: According to divination, this is a blessing for the state.

sentences.zh: 其五，七月內，熒惑守羽林，九月七日已退舍。

translations.literal: Fifth: within the seventh month Mars stayed in Yulin; by the seventh day of the ninth month it had withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth: within the seventh month Mars lingered in Yulin, and by the seventh day of the ninth month it had withdrawn from its station.

sentences.zh: 依占，不出三日，賊必敗散。

translations.literal: According to divination, within three days the rebels will surely be defeated and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: According to divination, within three days the enemy will surely be defeated and scattered.

sentences.zh: 其六，去年十一月二十日夜，有流星赤如火，從東北向西南，落賊帥盧明月營，破其橦車。

translations.literal: Sixth: on the night of the twentieth of the eleventh month last year, a meteor red as fire flowed from northeast to southwest and fell on the camp of rebel chief Lu Mingyue, smashing his battering rams.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth: on the night of the twentieth of the eleventh month last year, a meteor red as fire passed from northeast to southwest and fell on the camp of the rebel chief Lu Mingyue, smashing his battering engines.

sentences.zh: 其七，十二月十五日夜，通漢鎮北有赤氣亘北方，突厥將亡之應也。

translations.literal: Seventh: on the night of the fifteenth of the twelfth month, north of Tonghan Fort a red vapor stretched across the north—a sign that the Turks will perish.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh: on the night of the fifteenth of the twelfth month, north of Tonghan Fort a red vapor stretched across the north—a sign that the Turks are about to perish.

sentences.zh: 依勘城錄，河南洛陽並當甲子，與乾元初九爻及上元甲子符合。

translations.literal: According to the Kan Cheng Lu, Henan and Luoyang both fall under jiazi, matching Qian's initial nine line and the Upper Origin jiazi.
translations.idiomatic: According to the Kan Cheng Lu, Henan and Luoyang both fall under jiazi, matching the initial nine line of Qian and the jiazi of the Upper Origin.

sentences.zh: 此是福地，永無所慮。

translations.literal: This is a land of fortune—forever without cause for worry.
translations.idiomatic: These are lands of good fortune, forever without cause for alarm.

sentences.zh: 旋觀往政，側聞前古，彼則異時間出，今則一朝總萃。

translations.literal: Turning to examine past reigns and what one hears of ancient times—then omens appeared at different times; now they have all gathered in a single morning.
translations.idiomatic: Looking back at past reigns and what one hears of antiquity, omens then appeared at separate times, but now they have all gathered in a single morning.

sentences.zh: 豈非天贊有道，助殲兇孽，方清九夷於東獩，沉五狄於北溟，告成岱岳，無為汾水。

translations.literal: Is this not Heaven aiding the Way, helping to exterminate evil rebels, about to pacify the nine Yi in the eastern wilds and sink the five Di in the northern sea, proclaiming success at Mount Tai, ruling without action like at Fen River?
translations.idiomatic: Is this not Heaven aiding the Way, helping to destroy the wicked rebels, about to pacify the nine Yi in the eastern wilds and sink the five Di in the northern sea, proclaim success at Mount Tai, and rule in non-action as at the Fen River?

sentences.zh: 書奏，帝大悅，超拜秘書令，親待逾昵。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted the emperor was greatly pleased, promoted him beyond precedent to Director of the Secretariat, and treated him with increasing intimacy.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor was greatly pleased, promoted him out of turn to Director of the Secretariat, and treated him with ever greater intimacy.

sentences.zh: 帝每欲征討，充皆預知之，乃假託星象，奬成帝意，在位者皆切患之。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor wished to launch a campaign, Chong always knew beforehand and would feign stellar signs to encourage the emperor's intent; those in office all bitterly resented it.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor wished to launch a campaign, Chong always knew it beforehand and would fabricate stellar signs to encourage the emperor's intent, to the bitter resentment of those in office.

sentences.zh: 宇文化及殺逆之際，并誅充，時年七十五。

translations.literal: At the time of Yuwen Huaji's regicide, Chong was also executed; he was seventy-five.
translations.idiomatic: At the time of Yuwen Huaji's regicide, Chong was executed as well; he was seventy-five.

sentences.zh: 【論】史臣曰：王劭爰自幼童，迄乎白首，好學不倦，究極羣書。

translations.literal: [Commentary] The historiographer says: Wang Shao from boyhood to white head never wearied of learning, exhausting the breadth of books.
translations.idiomatic: [Commentary] The historiographer says: From boyhood to white-haired old age, Wang Shao loved learning without weariness and pursued books to their utmost limits.

sentences.zh: 搢紳洽聞之士，無不推其博物。

translations.literal: Among gentry and the well-informed, none failed to praise his encyclopedic learning.
translations.idiomatic: Among the gentry and the widely informed, none failed to praise his encyclopedic learning.

sentences.zh: 雅好著述，久在史官，既撰齊書，兼修隋典。

translations.literal: He loved authorship, long served as historiographer, wrote the Book of Qi and also compiled the Sui records.
translations.idiomatic: He loved writing, long served as a historiographer, compiled the Book of Qi, and also worked on the Sui records.

sentences.zh: 好詭怪之說，尚委巷之談，文詞鄙穢，體統繁雜。

translations.literal: He favored weird tales and alley gossip; his language was coarse and filthy, his structure tangled and chaotic.
translations.idiomatic: He favored strange and monstrous tales and back-alley gossip; his language was coarse and foul, and his structure tangled and chaotic.

sentences.zh: 直愧南、董，才無遷、固，徒煩翰墨，不足觀採。

translations.literal: He shames Nan and Dong; his talent falls short of Qian and Gu—merely wasting ink, unworthy of attention.
translations.idiomatic: He falls far short of the integrity of Dong Hu and the southern annalists, and his talent does not reach Sima Qian and Ban Gu; he merely wasted ink and is not worth consulting.

sentences.zh: 袁充少在江左，初以警悟見稱，委質隋朝，更以玄象自命。

translations.literal: Yuan Chong in youth was in the Jiangzuo region, first praised for quick wit; once he submitted to Sui, he styled himself an expert in celestial signs.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Chong in his youth lived in the Jiangzuo region and was first praised for quick wit; once he submitted to Sui, he styled himself a master of celestial signs.

sentences.zh: 並要求時幸，干進務入。

translations.literal: Both sought the favor of the times and schemed for advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Both sought the favor of their age and schemed for advancement.

sentences.zh: 劭經營符瑞，雜以妖訛，充變動星占，謬增晷影。

translations.literal: Shao traded in portents and omens, mixing in delusion and error; Chong manipulated star divination and falsely inflated gnomon shadows.
translations.idiomatic: Shao trafficked in portents and omens, mixing in delusion and falsehood; Chong manipulated star divination and falsely inflated gnomon shadows.

sentences.zh: 厚誣天道，亂常侮眾，刑茲勿捨，其在斯乎！

translations.literal: Grave deceptions against Heaven's Way, disturbing constants and mocking the masses—the punishment that should not be spared—surely applies here!
translations.idiomatic: They grossly deceived Heaven's Way, disturbed the constant order, and mocked the people—the punishment that should not be spared surely falls upon them here!

sentences.zh: 且劭為河朔清流，充乃江南望族，乾沒榮利，得不以道，頹其家聲，良可歎息。

translations.literal: Moreover Shao was a pure-stream gentleman of the Yellow River north, Chong a leading clan of the Jiangnan region—both grasping glory and profit by unrighteous means, bringing their family names to ruin—a matter truly lamentable.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Shao was a pure-stream gentleman of the Yellow River north and Chong a leading clan of the Jiangnan region; both grasped glory and profit by unrighteous means and brought their family names to ruin—a matter truly lamentable.
